children: The Process of Making Goods Mobile and Alienable
使物品可移动、可让渡的过程

No commercial activity is possible unless a deep and durable dissymmetry has been established. On the one hand, there are the different agents involved in preparing and realizing commercial transactions; on the other hand, there are the goods destined to become merchandise. This distinction largely overlaps with the distinction between people and things that is foundational for Western law — without it, no market could exist. The great divide between entities to which rights and obligations apply and entities that are bearers of rights and obligations to each other authorizes the transfer of property rights in exchange for monetary payment; thus, this divide underlies the appropriation of goods by agents.

The appropriation may apply to the thing itself, conceived as an indivisible entity by Roman law. It may also apply to duly specified rights corresponding to particular uses and bringing out certain qualities of the thing, as in Anglo-Saxon law.

除非一种深刻而持久的不对称得以确立，否则任何商业活动都不可能进行。一方面，是参与筹备和实现商业交易的不同行动者；另一方面，是注定成为商品的物品。这一区分在很大程度上与西方法律视为基石的人与物的区分相重叠——没有这一区分，就不可能有市场。一方是权利与义务所适用的实体，另一方是彼此互为权利与义务承担者的实体，这两者之间的巨大分界，授权人们以货币支付为对价转让财产权；因此，这一分界构成了行动者占有物品的基础。
这种占有可以针对物本身——罗马法把物设想为一个不可分割的实体；也可以针对与特定用途相应、并凸显物之某些品质的、经过恰当界定的权利，正如盎格鲁-撒克逊法中的情形。

The distinction can appear indisputable because it is taken as substantive. Things are incapable of intentional actions and can be defined by their passivity: they are ready to become goods that are exchanged. This simple and obvious criterion allows for a first sorting, for instance, between a car (the thing) and its owner (the person, the physical or legal entity), or between the prototype (the thing) and the engineer (the person) who designs it. Indeed, other than in a metaphorical sense, who would dare claim that the car or the model can own their owner or their designer or use them to develop their own programs of action?
这一区分之所以显得无可争辩，是因为它被当作实体性的区分。物不可能有意图的行动，可以用其被动性来定义：它们随时可以成为被交换的物品。这个简单而明显的标准允许进行最初的分类，例如在汽车（物）与其所有者（人，即自然人或法人）之间，或在原型机（物）与设计它的工程师（人）之间作出区分。的确，除了在隐喻意义上，谁又敢声称汽车或模型能够拥有它的主人或设计者，或利用他们来展开自己的行动纲领呢？

Yet this distinction is becoming less and less clear, or to put it another way, more and more difficult to establish and impose. The connected cars being brought to market by some companies are blurring boundaries. Heavy investments in both legal work and technology are required to establish and enforce, in this case, a clear separation between drivers and their car. With the increasing role played by artificial intelligence, these situations are multiplying. This is why this book adopts an altogether different position. I recognize the fundamental importance of the great divide, yet I refuse to consider it as self-evident. Based on countless studies by my colleagues and me on the relationships between people and things, we famously concluded that the distinction and asymmetry between entities destined to become commodities and the entities qualified as agents are not givens. What we showed, through detailed empirical studies, is that agents and goods get separated out and endowed with rights and responsibilities through a consequential set of processes. These processes can be long, often costly, and are made up of a multitude of trials to overcome and problems to be solved. The result is always fragile and temporary.

然而，这一区分正变得越来越不清晰，或者换个说法，越来越难以确立和推行。一些公司推向市场的联网汽车正在模糊边界。在此情形中，要在驾驶者与其汽车之间确立并执行清晰的分离，需要在法律工作与技术两方面投入大量资源。随着人工智能发挥越来越大的作用，这类情形正在成倍增加。正因如此，本书采取一种完全不同的立场。我承认这一巨大分界具有根本的重要性，但我拒绝把它视为不言自明的东西。基于我和同事围绕人与物关系所做的大量研究，我们得出了一个广为人知的结论：注定成为商品的实体与被界定为行动者的实体之间的区分与不对称，并不是既定的。我们通过细致的经验研究揭示的是：行动者与物品是经过一系列具有后果的过程才被分离出来，并被赋予权利与责任的。这些过程可能漫长、往往代价高昂，由大量有待克服的考验和有待解决的问题构成。其结果始终脆弱而短暂。

Economic or sociological studies that implicitly refer to what I have called interface markets have one main virtue: they, too, underline the foundational and structuring character of the distinction in markets. Once the necessity of the asymmetry has been posited, however, the principal limit of these kinds of studies is that they lose interest in the processes and in the instabilities that affect these processes. Although the existence of process is not denied, the numerous costly and uncertain activities associated with it are considered to be outside the market and thought not to interfere with its functioning.
那些隐含地参照我所称的界面市场的经济学或社会学研究，有一个主要优点：它们也强调这一区分在市场中具有奠基性和结构性的特征。然而，一旦不对称的必要性被设定，这类研究的主要局限就在于，它们对过程以及影响过程的不稳定性失去了兴趣。尽管过程的存在并未被否认，与过程相关的大量昂贵而不确定的活动却被视为处于市场之外，并被认为不会干扰市场的运行。

Market agencement makes this process the central question — and that is why it is here that I begin. The activities involved in design, manufacture, and commercialization that lead to the constitution of an always fragile and problematic disentangling of people and things are not dismissed as being external to market activities. They are instead at the center of what it means to establish a market. These activities develop according to two complementary logics. On the one hand, there is everything that corresponds to what I will call the
market-oriented passiva(c)tion

of goods. On the other hand, there is the whole set of mechanisms that establish agents capable of evaluating, calculating, deciding, or implementing courses of action, as we will see later, in Chapter 3.
市场装配把这一过程当作核心问题——这正是我由此开始的原因。设计、制造与商业化所涉及的活动，导致人与物之间始终脆弱而充满问题的解缠得以形成；这些活动并不被当作外在于市场活动的东西而打发掉，相反，它们处于“建立一个市场”这一事业的核心。这些活动依照两种互补的逻辑展开。一方面，是一切对应于我将称之为物品的“
面向市场的被动化
”（passiva(c)tion）的东西；另一方面，是一整套机制，它们确立起能够评估、计算、决策或实施行动方案的行动者——我们将在后面的第3章看到这一点。

My specific aim in this chapter is to understand how the activity of a thing can be directed and controlled while being rendered mobile and alienable. It is devoted to the analysis of the puzzling processes that can transform an entity of any kind into a good that can become a commodity. In order to move forward in exploring this enigma, I start from anthropological work that advances our understanding of these mechanisms. It is worth noting that economic anthropology does not always break with some of the fundamental hypotheses of interface markets, notably, the thesis of which is that that the world of goods and the world of agents can be described separately. Despite those limits, if appropriately reworked, some of the analytical tools developed by this discipline will prove useful. Consequently, as I make reference to older works of anthropology, the reader should not assume that I fully endorse the analyses proposed. First of all, because the problems anthropologists once dealt with were different from mine, but more importantly, because as with any good scientific work, the most important part is the methods and concepts they provide. In what follows, I am most interested in discovering useful methods and concepts.

本章的具体目标，是理解如何在使物变得可移动、可让渡的同时，引导并控制物的活动。本章致力于分析那些令人困惑的过程：它们能把任何一种实体转化为可以成为商品的物品。为了推进对这一谜题的探索，我从人类学研究中出发，这些研究增进了我们对上述机制的理解。值得注意的是，经济人类学并不总是与界面市场的某些基本假设决裂，尤其是这样一个论点：物品的世界与行动者的世界可以分开描述。尽管有这些局限，如果加以适当改造，这一学科所发展的某些分析工具仍将证明是有用的。因此，当我援引较早的人类学著作时，读者不应以为我完全赞同其中提出的分析。首先，因为人类学家当年处理的问题与我的问题不同；但更重要的是，因为与任何优秀的科学工作一样，最重要的部分是他们提供的方法与概念。在下文中，我最感兴趣的正是发现有用的方法与概念。

In the first part of the chapter, I present the main concepts that make it possible to follow the process of passiva(c)tion of goods. In a second part, I will then apply the proposed analysis to categories of goods reputed to resist merchandization, such as so-called fictitious commodities, or, among others, living beings. Finally, I insist on some of the concerns that the market-oriented passiva(c)tion process may generate.
在本章第一部分，我将呈现一些主要概念，它们使我们能够追踪物品被动化的过程。第二部分，我将把所提出的分析应用于若干据说抵抗商品化的物品类别，例如所谓的虚构商品，或诸多例子中的生命体。最后，我将强调面向市场的被动化过程可能引发的一些关切。
I. The Process of Market Passiva(c)tion
一、市场被动化的过程
SPACES OF CIRCULATION AND THE CAREERS OF GOODS
流通空间与物品的生涯
In interface markets, although they may have been difficult to define, the goods are given, and their properties are stable.
在界面市场中，物品尽管可能难以界定，却是既定的，其属性也是稳定的。

However simple and convincing it is, this perspective is untenable. It chooses to ignore that some entities are being denied the right and the possibility of becoming commodities, sometimes after enduring controversies, and conversely, to ignore the fact that well-established commodities might be violently contested.

It also disregards that other things reach the state of goods only at the end of long processes, over the course of which they transform and change status multiple times. In one interaction, they are goods; in another, they are gifts for relatives, until they end up, after several avatars, in huge dumps, from whence they are recycled and sold as spare parts to interested industries. It is difficult to settle for analyzing the ways markets function as though these transformations, these perpetual changes in status, did not exist. They cannot simply be taken for granted.
然而，无论这一视角多么简单、多么有说服力，它都站不住脚。它选择无视：某些实体被剥夺了成为商品的权利与可能性，有时这还是在一番争议之后；反过来，它也选择无视：一些稳固确立的商品可能遭到激烈争议。
它还无视另一些物只有在漫长过程结束时才达到物品状态，而在此过程中，它们多次转化并改变身份。在一次互动中，它们是物品；在另一次互动中，它们是送给亲戚的礼物；直到历经几番变形之后，它们最终进入巨大的垃圾场，又从那里被回收，作为零配件卖给感兴趣的产业。人们很难满足于分析市场的运作方式，仿佛这些转化、这些身份的无休止变化并不存在。它们不能被简单地视为理所当然。
SPACES OF CIRCULATION

In economic anthropology, one of the first solutions imagined to explain how the status of a commercial good is acquired was to introduce the notion of the space (or sphere) of circulation. Strongly inspired by Karl Marx and Marcel Mauss, this body of work is closely linked to the notions of systems of exchange and cultural systems. In general, these studies took a comparative approach and probed the differences between Western and non-Western societies.
流通空间
在经济人类学中，最早用来解释商业物品之身份如何获得的解决方案之一，是引入流通空间（或流通领域）的概念。这一研究传统深受卡尔·马克思（Karl Marx）与马塞尔·莫斯（Marcel Mauss）启发，与交换体系和文化体系的概念紧密相连。总体而言，这些研究采取比较方法，探究西方社会与非西方社会之间的差异。

In Marx’s analysis, there exists a sort of structural abyss between Western capitalist society and other economies that either preceded it or developed in other parts of the world. In the Western economy, everything may become a commodity when there is a prospect of profit and accumulation (work and land are no exception), while other economies were perceived to contain the expansion of the market sphere. Drawing on the opposition between gift and commodity, Mauss contributed to exploring this discontinuity, this radical opposition between capitalist and noncapitalist economies. He showed that it depended on the existence of fundamentally different systems of exchange and therefore of sociability. For decades, exploring different regimes of the circulation of goods, those characterized as commercial and those characterized as noncommercial, was one of economic anthropology’s favorite themes.

在马克思的分析中，西方资本主义社会与或者先于它、或者在世界其他地区发展起来的其他经济之间，存在某种结构性深渊。在西方经济中，只要存在利润与积累的前景，一切都可以成为商品（劳动与土地也不例外）；而其他经济则被认为遏制了市场领域的扩张。借助礼物与商品的对立，莫斯参与了对这种断裂、对资本主义经济与非资本主义经济之间这一根本对立的探索。他表明，这种断裂取决于存在根本不同的交换体系，因而也取决于存在根本不同的社会交往体系。数十年来，探讨物品流通的不同体制——被界定为商业性的体制与被界定为非商业性的体制——一直是经济人类学最钟爱的主题之一。
One of the most impactful theses was developed by Paul Bohannan in his 1955 study of the circulation of different types of goods in West Africa.

According to Bohannan, the goods exchanged among the Tiv in Nigeria can be classified in three large categories, which correspond to distinct spheres of exchange. One sphere concerns subsistence goods; another, goods that constitute the wealth of their holders (bracelets, herds, slaves); the third is made up of marriageable women. Exchanges are possible within each sphere, or, if you prefer, between the goods that belong to the same category. Exchanges are very difficult or even forbidden between distinct spheres; this is particularly the case insofar as no unified currency generally exists. Other studies have empirically attempted to confirm the existence of spheres of exchange in a great number of societies. Goods, depending on the category to which they belong, are destined to circulate in spaces that are separate from one another.
最具影响力的论点之一，是保罗·博安南（Paul Bohannan）在1955年对西非不同类型物品流通的研究中提出的。

按照博安南的说法，尼日利亚蒂夫人（Tiv）之间交换的物品可分为三大类，分别对应于不同的交换领域。一个领域涉及生计物品；另一个领域涉及构成其持有者财富的物品（手镯、畜群、奴隶）；第三个领域由可婚配的女性构成。交换可以在每个领域内部进行，或者如果你愿意，也可以说在属于同一类别的物品之间进行。在不同领域之间，交换极其困难，甚至被禁止；尤其因为通常不存在统一货币，情况更是如此。其他研究则在经验上试图证实交换领域在大量社会中的存在。物品根据其所属类别，注定要在彼此分离的空间中流通。

These observations were originally made in non-Western societies, but have since been extended to the West, notably to underline the existence of commercial and noncommercial spheres between which circulation is made difficult. For example, Maurice Bloch and Jonathan Parry consider the family a site that has been protected from the invasion of the market, at least up to a certain era.

One could also cite work that aligns with the analyses of Karl Polanyi, Marshall Sahlins, or Marcel Mauss and insists upon the existence of spaces and goods that resist commodification for moral, political, or even economic reasons. The things that escape the market will vary, depending on historical eras and societies. Some contemporary societies, for instance, show great hesitation in allowing blood, organs, or fundamental scientific knowledge to enter the market sphere. When exchange appears to be the only possible option, other than pure gift or predation,
they will only enter into commercial exchange depending upon the spaces of circulation in which they take place.
这些观察最初是在非西方社会中作出的，但后来被扩展到西方，尤其是为了强调商业领域与非商业领域的存在，而二者之间的流通十分困难。例如，莫里斯·布洛赫（Maurice Bloch）与乔纳森·帕里（Jonathan Parry）把家庭视为一个至少在某些时代受到保护、免遭市场入侵的场所。
人们也可以举出与卡尔·波兰尼（Karl Polanyi）、马歇尔·萨林斯（Marshall Sahlins）或马塞尔·莫斯的分析相一致、并坚持认为存在因道德、政治甚至经济理由而抵抗商品化的空间与物品的著作。逃脱市场的物会因历史时代与社会而不同。例如，一些当代社会在允许血液、器官或基础科学知识进入市场领域方面表现出极大犹豫。当交换显得是除纯粹赠予或掠夺之外唯一可能的选择时，
它们是否进入商业交换，仍取决于交换发生在何种流通空间之中。

These different analyses share a single hypothesis. They all rest on the idea that it is always possible, in principle, at least, to shield certain goods from commodification by including them in systems of social relations and institutional frameworks that forbid it. It bears repeating that the distinction is not between entities that are
naturally
passive and would be inevitably destined, whatever one did, to become commodities at some point, and entities that are
naturally
active (agents) and would seize them for profit, but rather between spaces that are
socially

constituted and impose their rules on circulation. This idea of spaces of circulation and specific exchange systems that confer a certain status on things is a first step in the direction of process goods. To become a commodity, the thing must be torn out of the world to which it is attached and displaced in order to then be reassigned to a new world. Certain moves, certain transitions from one sphere to another, from one space to another, are made impossible or very costly. Thus, certain goods or certain beings are not exchangeable. They must be kept, and they are kept. To take another example of which economists are fond, in contemporary societies, children who are unhappy with their parents, even if they wanted to, would have real difficulty in getting rid of them and exchanging them for better fathers or mothers or selling them to whomever would be willing to buy them. In a country such as France, the commercialization of children (and indeed also of parents) is taboo: one can adopt them, but one cannot buy them.
这些不同的分析共享同一个假设。它们都立足于这样一种观念：至少在原则上，总有可能通过把某些物品纳入禁止商品化的社会关系体系与制度框架，使它们免受商品化。值得重复的是，这一区分并不发生在两类实体之间——一类
