Of course, those who develop commercial goods can find ways to free themselves, to a certain extent, from these complementary investments by playing on the qualities of the goods. For instance, a car designed to not require any cooling liquid could function without the infrastructure organized to make this liquid widely available. Yet no matter how ingenious the engineers who created such a car, it would still require the constitution of some associated milieu — some form of roadway — even a crude one, pared down to just a few elements. Without it, no passiva(c)tion is imaginable, no vehicle that is both autonomous and controllable can exist, and as a consequence, commodification is not possible. It is only in an arbitrary manner, always open to dispute, that rights are attributed exclusively to the developers and producers of the good in question. In fact, the entire set of agents who participated, in a necessarily coordinated way, in the constitution of that good and its associated milieu should be considered. Answers can be examined only on a case-by-case basis. And it appears that with the attempts to commercialize living beings and digital data, they are becoming increasingly debatable and complex. In many situations, to identify Agent A, the entity that gets property rights and who will therefore be entitled to transfer them to Agent B, is a long and hazardous journey. Identifying the rights that will be commuted is a first challenge. A second challenge is to determine who conceived of the good and to accept that they be the sole legitimate bearer of these rights. This deserves a word of explanation.

这类困难有一个显而易见的根源。关联环境必须被精心而合宜地设计与制造，才能使物品的解缠及其不间断运作成为可能。一辆大众高尔夫（Volkswagen Golf）行驶在受交通法规管辖的高速公路网络上；一个孩子把全部积蓄花在一台 iPod 上，但如果没有 iTunes，这台 iPod 就无法串流歌曲；保育员来到一个事先布置好的环境，这一环境使保育员得以提供照护。提供环境需要劳动、灵感，以及大量汗水。当然，商业物品的开发者可以借助物品的品质做文章，找到办法在某种程度上摆脱这些互补性投资。例如，一辆被设计为不需要任何冷却液的汽车，可以在没有那种为使冷却液广泛可得而组织起来的基础设施的情况下运行。然而，无论创造这样一辆汽车的工程师多么精巧，它仍然需要某种关联环境的构成——某种形式的道路，哪怕十分粗糙、被精简到仅剩少数要素。没有它，任何被动化都无从想象，任何既自主又可控的车辆都无法存在，商品化因而也不可能。人们只是以任意的方式——而且始终可以争论——才把权利排他性地归于所涉物品的开发者和生产者。事实上，应当考虑的是所有以必然协调的方式参与了该物品及其关联环境之构成的行动者。答案只能逐案考察。而看来，随着把生命体与数字数据商业化的尝试，这些答案正变得越来越可争议、越来越复杂。在许多情况下，指认行动者 A——那个获得财产权、因而有权将其转让给行动者 B 的实体——是一段漫长而危险的旅程。指认将被转换的权利，是第一项挑战。第二项挑战是确定谁构想了该物品，并接受他们是这些权利唯一合法的承载者。这值得略作解释。

The history of property rights shows us that the controversies born of this paradox — dissociating those who develop the goods and those who develop the associated milieu — are enduring. Consider, for instance, the well-known late eighteenth-century debates around the birth of copyright law, which involved the attribution of authorship.
Who is the author of
The Barber of Seville
or
La religieuse

? How can paternity of a work be attributed to a single person, when it is easily shown that it was composed by borrowing and plagiarism? Along the same lines: Is it reasonable to consider that Newton is the author of the laws of gravitation and of the
Principia

, when it is obvious that if someone really has to be responsible, it can only be God himself, the God Newton admits to serving to as a technical assistant? There are associated milieus from which the works cannot be detached: in the first case, the crowd of anonymous people who contributed to the emergence of Figaro as a character; in the second case, God or nature. It requires a juridical fiction (or convention), plausible, but circumstantial, to decide that Beaumarchais and Diderot are the authors, forgetting those who prepared the ground, whereas Newton is only the discoverer, the wise explorer of a work whose paternity escapes him completely. Newton, Einstein, or Watson and Crick only elucidate laws they had no hand in constituting, whereas Edison, Diesel, or Craig Venter created objects that did not exist before them: the filament bulb for the first, an effective motor for the second, and synthesized DNA for the third.
财产权的历史告诉我们，由这一悖论——把开发物品的人与开发关联环境的人分离开来——所生的争议是持久的。例如，不妨想想18世纪末围绕版权法诞生而展开的那些著名辩论，它们涉及作者身份的归属。
《塞维利亚的理发师》（
The Barber of Seville
）或《修女》（
La religieuse
）的作者是谁？当人们可以轻易表明一部作品是靠借用与剽窃写成时，又怎能把它的作者身份归于单独一个人？沿着同样的思路：认为牛顿（Newton）是万有引力定律和《原理》（
Principia

）的作者，是否合理？毕竟很明显，如果真的必须有人负责，那只能是上帝本人——那个牛顿承认自己只是作为技术助手为之服务的上帝。存在着作品无法从中脱离的关联环境：在前一种情形中，是那群促成费加罗（Figaro）这一人物诞生的无名大众；在后一种情形中，是上帝或自然。需要一种法律拟制（或惯例）——它看似可信，却依赖具体情境——才能断定博马舍（Beaumarchais）和狄德罗（Diderot）是作者，并遗忘那些奠定基础的人；与此同时，牛顿只是发现者，是一部作品的睿智探索者，而这部作品的作者身份完全不属于他。牛顿、爱因斯坦（Einstein），或沃森与克里克（Watson and Crick），只是阐明他们并未参与构成的规律；而爱迪生（Edison）、狄塞尔（Diesel）或克雷格·文特尔（Craig Venter）则创造了他们之前并不存在的对象：对第一位来说是灯丝灯泡，对第二位来说是一台高效的发动机，对第三位来说是合成 DNA。

In the case of scientific discovery, the entity is considered to be indiscernible from the associated milieu that completely absorbs it. Although we can name the scientists who made the discovery, no property right can be attached to their findings. The case of invention or creation turns out differently. The entity can become a good because it does not dissolve into its associated milieu, and it is therefore possible (thanks to such legal fictions as legal persons) to identify, from among the many who may have participated in the invention, the small number to whom property rights will be attributed. Depending on the goods, these fictions turn out to be more or less robust and more or less up to the task of garnering a double recognition: that the good was developed independently of its associated milieu and that those who develop it can be identified without ambiguity.

就科学发现而言，实体被认为与完全吞没它的关联环境无法分辨。尽管我们可以说出作出发现的科学家的名字，却没有任何财产权可以附着于他们的发现。发明或创造的情形则不同。实体能够成为物品，因为它没有消融于其关联环境之中；因此，（借助法人这类法律拟制）有可能从可能参与发明的众多人中，指认出将获得财产权的那少数人。取决于具体物品，这些拟制或多或少较为稳固，也或多或少足以完成一项双重承认：物品是独立于其关联环境发展出来的，而开发它的人可以被毫无歧义地指认出来。

In the case of a car, it is somewhat easier to draw distinctions. There is a collection of human beings at a car company who, with the help of tools, instruments, and machines, bring the car from the drawing board to the shop floor, to prototyping platforms, to the production units, and finally to sales sites. There is also a set of actors who contribute to realizing the public and private infrastructures that allow the automobile to circulate and accomplish the actions for which it was conceived. The situation becomes more complicated, however, when it comes to introducing a new kind of vehicle into the existing milieu. The current milieu is not adapted to supporting a market for electric cars, which have different fueling and maintenance requirements than those with combustion engines. Think also of so-called “self-driving vehicles” and the heavily complex associated milieus they require. These vehicles may circulate only if the moral, technical, economic, legal, and town-planning concerns have been satisfactorily resolved.
Every radical innovation highlights the need to (re)build a world that will allow a novel good to exist and to develop unhindered.

就汽车而言，作出区分要容易一些。一家汽车公司里有一群人，他们借助工具、仪器和机器，把汽车从绘图板带到车间，带到原型平台，带到生产单元，最终带到销售网点。还有一组行动者，他们参与建成公共与私人基础设施，使汽车得以通行，并完成汽车被构想出来所要完成的行动。然而，当要把一种新型车辆引入既有环境时，情况就变得更复杂。当前的环境并不适合支撑电动汽车市场，因为电动汽车在燃料补给与维护方面的要求不同于内燃机汽车。也不妨想想所谓“自动驾驶汽车”以及它们所需的极为复杂的关联环境。只有在道德、技术、经济、法律和城市规划方面的关切都得到令人满意的解决之后，这些车辆才可能通行。
每一项激进的创新都凸显出（重新）建造一个世界的必要性，这个世界将使一种新颖物品得以存在并不受阻碍地发展。

With the development of digital technologies and biotechnologies, these different operations — the separation between the good and its associated milieu and the determination of the rights bearers — become more elusive. The legal conventions that justified them are under pressure and have to be reconsidered on a case-by-case basis. Each new good leads back to the following fundamental questions: What is its associated milieu? What are the forces that structure and organize it? How can the uses that can be attached to a good be identified and to which agents can their conception be attributed? In sum, marketing goods always leads to rehashing the debate that raged three centuries ago. There may be less talk of God, of the creator and his creation, but more of nature and its autoregulation mechanisms; there is less talk of literary works, but more on lines of code, or the syntax of computer languages, or the translation of the genome into genetic information. Despite these changes, the same questions persist. And if no satisfying answer is given, the market-oriented passiva(c)tion of goods, the one that detaches them, frames their courses of action, and organizes the transfer of property rights, is curtailed.

随着数字技术与生物技术的发展，这些不同的操作——物品与其关联环境之间的分离，以及权利承载者的确定——变得更加难以捉摸。为这些操作提供正当性的法律惯例正承受压力，必须逐案重新审视。每一件新物品都把人带回以下根本问题：它的关联环境是什么？有哪些力量在构造和组织这一环境？可以附着于一件物品的用途如何被指认，而这些用途的构想又可归于哪些行动者？总之，营销物品总是导致重新翻炒三个世纪前激烈进行的那场辩论。也许人们较少谈论上帝、造物主及其造物，而更多谈论自然及其自我调节机制；较少谈论文学作品，而更多谈论代码行、计算机语言的句法，或基因组向遗传信息的转译。尽管有这些变化，同样的问题依然存在。而如果没有给出令人满意的答案，物品的面向市场的被动化——那种使物品脱离、框定其行动过程并组织财产权转让的被动化——就会受阻。

When a start-up cranks out lines of code to develop new applications or software as a service, when it encrypts confidential data to avoid being hacked, it is only one active element in a network of high-powered mathematicians, companies, or groups of software engineers whose productions it constantly draws on and that in return feed off what it produces and makes available. It must be added that the mesh of the milieu in which software services function is heightened by the success of the open-source movement.

In this case, each service provided and its associated milieu is the result of a collective and continuous process that makes it difficult to distinguish them, that scrambles both the attribution of property rights and their distribution among those who develop the good and those who develop the associated milieu. The legal convention that supposed a decoupling and a desynchronization of innovations (those that concern the goods and those that concern the associated milieu) then loses credibility and efficacy. That is no doubt why the commodification of these services has generated suggestions for changing or adapting property rights. There is notably a gradual sliding from the conception of property as an absolute right of a person to a thing to a conception of property as depending on a bundle of rights connecting the owner to other people through a complex set of social and legal relations that run through the asset.

当一家初创企业源源不断地写出代码行，以开发新的应用程序或软件即服务（software as a service），当它加密机密数据以防被黑客入侵时，它只是一个网络中的活跃要素，这个网络由高水平的数学家、公司或软件工程师群体组成；它不断汲取他们的产出，而他们反过来也靠它生产并提供的东西获得滋养。还必须补充说，软件服务运作于其中的环境之网，因开源运动（open-source movement）的成功而变得更加绵密。

在这种情形中，每项提供的服务及其关联环境，都是一个集体而持续的过程的结果；这一过程使二者难以区分，打乱了财产权的归属，也打乱了财产权在开发物品者与开发关联环境者之间的分配。那种假定创新（涉及物品的创新与涉及关联环境的创新）彼此解耦、去同步化的法律惯例，于是失去了可信性与效力。这无疑正是这些服务的商品化催生出改变或调整财产权之建议的原因。尤其可以看到一种逐渐的滑移：从把财产视为一个人对一物的绝对权利的观念，滑向另一种观念，即财产取决于一束权利，这束权利通过贯穿资产的一组复杂社会与法律关系，把所有者与他人连接起来。

In my research on patents, the development of nonhuman beings such as animals, plants, or microorganisms as market goods has provided the ideal example on which to examine these issue of property rights in detail. Consider, for instance, the recent development of new “assisted” or “targeted” techniques of mutagenesis. These are increasingly used to mold the genetic profile of certain plants in order to make them able to withstand drought or certain herbicides, produce medical molecules, or facilitate their conservation. Whereas pure and simple transgenesis involves introducing a new gene in a plant, whose qualities are thus artificially transformed, assisted mutagenesis solicits the active and constant collaboration of Mother Nature. Mutagenesis is a phenomenon that occurs spontaneously when plants reproduce. However, the resulting mutations are infrequent and very random. Under these conditions, why not help nature by guiding the process, instead of entrusting everything to chance? This little boost requires knowledge and elaborate techniques, especially when it is a matter of localizing and identifying the genes involved in producing particular agronomic, organoleptic, or medicinal characteristics that have been judged of interest.

在我关于专利的研究中，把动物、植物或微生物这类非人存在者开发为市场物品，为细致考察这些财产权问题提供了理想范例。例如，不妨考虑晚近发展起来的“辅助”或“定向”诱变新技术。这些技术越来越多地被用来塑造某些植物的遗传特征，使它们能够耐旱或耐受某些除草剂、产生药用分子，或便于保存。纯粹而简单的转基因技术是在植物中引入一个新基因，植物的品质因此被人工改造；辅助诱变则求得大自然母亲积极而持续的协作。诱变是植物繁殖时自发发生的一种现象。然而，由此产生的突变十分稀少，而且极为随机。在这些条件下，为什么不通过引导这一过程来帮助自然，而不是把一切交给偶然？这一小小的助推需要知识和精细的技术，尤其当事情涉及定位并识别那些参与产生某些被认为有价值的农艺、感官或药用特征的基因时。

In what follows, I would like to consider a special case of a broccoli genetically modified to enhance its cancer-prevention properties. The lengthy and eventful story of its design is interesting and exemplary. This singular broccoli is the distant result of crossbreeding done in the 1980s between a cultivated broccoli and a wild broccoli from the south of Italy. Not only does it taste good — it also contains exceptional levels of glucoraphanin, a nutrient that develops antioxidant enzymes. In this particular case, before the cross was made, the broccoli genome had to be sequenced, and the genes responsible for the properties being sought had to be localized and identified. This cross could have happened in a natural way. Even if the probability of such an event is extremely low, it is not zero. What the breeder does is to take a possibility nature might produce and make it happen with certainty in a controlled fashion.

在下文中，我想考察一个特殊案例：一种经过基因改造、以增强其防癌特性的西兰花。其设计过程漫长而曲折，故事既有意思又堪称典范。这种独一的西兰花，是20世纪80年代将一种栽培西兰花与意大利南部的一种野生西兰花杂交所留下的遥远结果。它不仅味道好，而且含有异常高水平的萝卜硫苷（glucoraphanin），这是一种能促生抗氧化酶的养分。在这个特殊案例中，在进行杂交之前，必须先对西兰花基因组进行测序，并定位和识别负责所需特性的基因。这次杂交本可以自然发生。即使这类事件发生的概率极低，也并非为零。育种者所做的，是把自然可能产生的一种可能性拿来，以受控方式使它确定地发生。

The contrast with pure and simple transgenesis is striking. In both cases, the developer of new seeds performs a gesture that is inscribed in a long lineage of prior investments, some of which go all the way back to the neolithic age, that have led the variety on which the breeder is working to its current state through repeated crossing and selecting. These investments flow from both human work and the work of nature. By introducing a foreign gene, radical transgenesis provokes a deep break in the course of this history. It detaches the plant from a past and a milieu in which nature played the main part, humans merely accompanying and orienting it. In its gentlest forms, assisted mutagenesis, in contrast, maintains and prolongs the entanglements from which novelty and diversity emerge without discombobulating the composition of the hybrid collectives, composed of human beings and natural entities, that piloted evolution to that point. To put it in an image, the elaboration of a new variety can in one case easily be attributed, at least in the main, to the scientists and engineers, whereas in the second, it is part of a natural history in which humans bear only a small portion of responsibility. To put it differently, with transgenesis, the plant is ripped out of its traditional associated milieu and is endowed with a new associated milieu manufactured in a lab and then controlled, insofar as possible, by the scientists and engineers; with assisted mutagenesis, the associated world, its modes of organization and its rules of functioning are preserved, at least in part, since the experts are only hastening the passiva(c)tion process. In the first case, it is not illegitimate to consider that the property rights can be attributed to the teams who did the work and, therefore, given the work contracts that cover this, to the companies that employ them: the associated milieu required by the transgenic plant is largely composed of the scientific and technical infrastructure (laboratories, field experiments, simulations, and so on) necessary for their conception, development, and monitoring and therefore does not depend too much on other agents, notably those who consider that the only legitimate option, both moral and technical, is to cooperate with Mother Nature. Transgenesis is a technique of passiva(c)tion that can be directly articulated with the commercial circuit and with bilateral commercial transactions. In the second case, the forces that contribute to the emergence of the new variety are distributed between the scientists and engineers, on the one hand, and nature, on the other, in such a way that it is problematic to separate what comes from whom in the creation of the new variety. Transgenesis draws heavily on human creativity, whereas assisted mutagenesis rests largely on nature’s creativity.

与纯粹而简单的转基因技术的对照十分鲜明。在两种情形中，新种子的开发者所做的举动，都铭刻在一条漫长的先前投资谱系之中——其中一些投资一直追溯到新石器时代——这些投资通过反复杂交与选择，使育种者所操作的品种达到当前状态。这些投资既来自人类的劳作，也来自自然的劳作。通过引入一个外源基因，激进的转基因技术在这一历史进程中造成深深的断裂。它使植物脱离一个过去与一个环境，在那里，自然扮演主要角色，人类只是伴随并引导它。相反，在其最温和的形式中，辅助诱变则维持并延长那些产生新颖性与多样性的纠缠，而不打乱此前一直引导演化至此的混合集体的构成——这些混合集体由人类存在者与自然实体组成。打个比方，在一种情形中，新品种的培育至少大体上可以轻易归功于科学家和工程师；而在第二种情形中，它则属于一部自然史，人类只承担一小部分责任。换种说法：借助转基因技术，植物被从其传统的关联环境中撕扯出来，并被赋予一个新的关联环境——这个环境在实验室中制造，随后尽可能由科学家和工程师控制；借助辅助诱变，相关的世界、其组织模式及其运作规则至少部分得以保留，因为专家只是加速了被动化过程。在第一种情形中，认为财产权可以归于完成这项工作的团队、并因而（鉴于覆盖此项工作的劳动合同）归于雇用他们的公司，并非不正当：转基因植物所需的关联环境，主要由其构想、开发与监测所必需的科学技术基础设施（实验室、田间试验、模拟等等）构成，因此不太依赖其他行动者，尤其是那些认为唯一正当的选择——无论在道德上还是技术上——就是与大自然母亲合作的行动者。转基因技术是一种可以直接接入商业循环与双边商业交易的被动化技术。在第二种情形中，促成新品种涌现的力量一方面分布于科学家和工程师，另一方面分布于自然，其分布方式使我们在新品种的创造中难以区分何者来自谁。转基因技术大量汲取人类的创造力，而辅助诱变则主要依托自然的创造力。

Between these two extreme possibilities, there are a host of intermediary strategies that combine the intelligent cooperation of natural forces and human forces in variable proportions. In these circumstances, the difficulty of establishing who is the author of these transformations is such that the office charged with delivering patents cannot avoid debates worthy of the most eminent Scholastic tradition. Indeed, they have to determine the respective roles of natural determinism and human intervention, case by case, plant after plant. The problem raised is in fact that of distinguishing the forces that act on the good from the forces that act on its associated milieu. If you consider, for instance, that such and such a type of assisted mutation sets off “essentially” biological processes

— to pick up on the surprising terminology used in a 1998 European directive that sounds like unavowed reminiscences of the ancient philosophical theory according to which substances exist, that is to say, categories that precede all others — and, therefore, if it is mainly nature that produces
both
the good
and

its milieu, then it is presumed that it is nature that ensures the passiva(c)tion. The directive specifies that in this case, the production process cannot be patented; no property right can be attributed to the teams that produced this mutagenesis. If one decides, on the contrary, that the transformation is the result of a particularly ingenious technique (reaching beyond the operations of a traditional breeder who only organizes and channels the work of Mother Nature), appropriation becomes easier, since there is a creation by an industrious person of an original entity whose conception, as an autonomous and acting entity, can be dissociated from that of its associated milieu. This obviously applies to transgenesis that completely or almost completely breaks free from nature’s work: the gene can therefore be patented. Thus qualified, the good more easily enters commercial transactions, since the presence of these new qualities guarantees the attribution of rights and their permutation.

在这两种极端可能性之间，还存在大量中介策略，它们以不同比例把自然力量与人类力量的明智合作结合起来。在这些情况下，确定谁是这些转变的作者的困难之大，使负责授予专利的机构无法回避一些堪与最杰出的经院传统相媲美的辩论。的确，它们必须逐案、逐种植物地确定自然的决定作用与人为干预各自扮演的角色。所提出的问题，实际上是区分作用于物品的力量与作用于其关联环境的力量。例如，如果你认为某种类型的辅助突变触发了“本质上”的生物过程
——借用1998年一项欧洲指令所使用的令人惊讶的术语，这一术语听起来像是对一种古代哲学理论未加承认的回忆：按照该理论，实体存在，也就是说，存在着先于其他一切范畴的范畴——并因此认为，主要是自然生产了
物品及其环境

，那么就可以推定，是自然确保了被动化。该指令明确规定，在此情形中，生产过程不能获得专利；任何财产权都不能归于完成这种诱变的团队。反之，如果人们认定，这一转变是一项特别精巧的技术的产物（它超出了传统育种者的操作——后者只是组织和疏导大自然母亲的劳作），那么据为己有就变得更容易，因为这里存在一个勤勉之人对一个原创实体的创造，而这个实体作为一个自主且行动着的实体，其构想可以与对其关联环境的构想分离开来。这显然适用于完全或几乎完全摆脱自然劳作的转基因技术：基因因而可以获得专利。如此获得品质界定之后，物品更容易进入商业交易，因为这些新品质的存在保证了权利的归属及其置换。

Generalizing is easy. We can measure in this case how great a dilemma living beings set up, given the tension that they bring to the fore between passiva(c)tion and appropriation. This question is so complex that it is sometimes impossible to reach a clear and settled position, as shown by the recent twists in the anticancer broccoli saga. In March 2015, the Enlarged Board of Appeal of the European Patent Office ruled that plants stemming from essentially biological processes could be protected on condition that they fulfill the three requirements for obtaining a patent: novelty, inventiveness, and industrial applicability. In sum, in its ruling, the board says that the process cannot be subject to a patent, but that the plant that it produces (the asset) can be. This can seem a lame compromise, even though there are many arguments in its favor. One can, of course, consider that by accelerating and orienting nature’s course, humans participate in the creation of an entity that might never have seen the light of day, given how low the probability of that particular mutation is. This observation is enough to justify attributing property rights. Problems persist, however. The new variety is torn out of the natural milieu that allowed it to emerge and that is thus severed from a part of its creative power, since that variety, at least for the time it is protected by a patent, can no longer intervene in the constitution of new species. As popular wisdom has it, it is robbing Peter (nature) to pay Paul (Monsanto). Or to put it another way, this comes down to inciting Paul to innovate, but discouraging Peter from doing the same. Who can evaluate the consequences of this decision, which can only be arbitrary, in terms of efficiency or social well-being?

由此推广开去很容易。在此我们可以衡量，生命体造成了多么巨大的两难，因为它们凸显出被动化与占有之间的张力。这个问题如此复杂，以至于有时不可能达成清晰而确定的立场，抗癌西兰花传奇近来的曲折便是明证。2015年3月，欧洲专利局（European Patent Office）扩大上诉委员会（Enlarged Board of Appeal）裁定，源自本质上生物学过程的植物可以获得保护，条件是它满足获得专利的三项要求：新颖性、创造性与工业实用性。总之，该委员会在裁决中说，过程不能成为专利的对象，但它所产生的植物（资产）可以。这看起来可能是一个蹩脚的妥协，尽管有许多论据支持它。当然，人们可以认为，通过加速并引导自然的进程，人类参与创造了一个可能永远不会问世的实体，因为那种特定突变发生的概率如此之低。这一观察足以证成财产权的归属。然而，问题依然存在。新品种被从其得以涌现的自然环境中撕扯出来，而这个环境因此被切断了其一部分创造力，因为该品种——至少在其受专利保护期间——不再能参与新物种的构成。正如民间智慧所说，这是抢彼得（自然）的钱来付给保罗（孟山都，Monsanto），亦即拆东墙补西墙。或者换种说法，这等于激励保罗创新，却抑制彼得做同样的事。谁能从效率或社会福利的角度，评估这一只能任意作出的决定的后果？
I do not want to get into a discussion about patent law because I will return to this elsewhere.

What I am interested in here are the issues the patenting process must address, which tend to be forgotten. To deal with all these issues, which concern the modalities of commodification of living beings, one would have to reexamine some of the foundations of property law, one at a time. The distinction between discovery and innovation made sense at the end of the eighteenth century, when it was a matter of tracing the limit between what accrues to man and what accrues to God or nature. It does not anymore. This absurdity is nowhere as blatant as in the realm of biotechnologies, as well as digital technologies. In the process of conceiving new beings, human and non-human entities are in tight collaboration, and it seems difficult not to take that into account in allocating property rights. In fact, not only does patent law rest on an outdated metaphysics, it moreover claims its economic justification on the basis of a theory of innovation that is oblivious to all the studies conducted since the end of the 1970s, studies that show how unrealistic the models are that deny the open, collective, iterative, and gradual character of innovation processes, especially in the case of biotechnologies. In avoiding the reality of passiva(c)tion devices, patent offices are hanging on to solutions that fall short of the considerable stakes that emerge with the commodification of the living.
我不想陷入关于专利法的讨论，因为我将在别处回到这个问题。

我在这里感兴趣的，是专利授予过程必须处理、却往往被遗忘的那些问题。要处理所有这些涉及生命体商品化方式的问题，人们将不得不逐一重新审视财产法的一些基础。发现与创新之间的区分，在18世纪末是有意义的，当时的事情是在归于人者与归于上帝或自然者之间划出界限。如今它已不再有意义。这种荒谬在生物技术以及数字技术领域表现得再明显不过。在构想新存在者的过程中，人类实体与非人实体紧密协作，而在分配财产权时，似乎很难不把这一点考虑在内。事实上，专利法不仅建立在一种过时的形而上学之上，它还依据一种创新理论来主张自身的经济正当性，而这种理论对20世纪70年代末以来进行的所有研究视而不见——这些研究表明，那些否认创新过程具有开放、集体、迭代与渐进特征的模型是多么不切实际，在生物技术的情形中尤其如此。专利局回避被动化装置的现实，固守着一些不足以应对生命体商品化所带来之重大利害的解决方案。

The urgent need to imagine new solutions is all the greater, given that the (debatable) legal arguments that push toward attributing property rights to the developers, by underestimating the part nature plays, increase the ontological uncertainties associated with the goods produced. The dilemma is striking: if nature’s participation is taken to have been essential, it becomes difficult to attach private rights to the newcomer, but the confidence in the future behavior of the new good is great. What is called “nature” is the name given to a long story over the course of which each new event has been stringently evaluated, and that is why it is a credible guarantor.
A contrario

, if this participation is considered secondary, then the organism in question can be more easily appropriated, but the fact that it is considered completely artificial makes its passiva(c)tion uncertain. Framing it, controlling its behavior, monitoring collateral damages thus become categorical imperatives; this requires considerable investments from the one who elaborated the new organism and who, having decided to forgo the regulatory mechanisms of Mother Nature insofar as possible, can be held responsible for the effects produced, whether they be judged good or bad. When, in order to facilitate market-oriented passiva(c)-tion, developers manipulate both the goods and their associated milieus, the latter constitute worlds that are (clandestinely) sold with the good without the slightest discussion. Under such conditions, it is not surprising that they provoke contestation and protests.
想象新解决方案的紧迫性之所以更大，是因为那些推动把财产权归于开发者的（可争议的）法律论据，通过低估自然所扮演的角色，增加了与所生产物品相关的本体论不确定性。两难十分醒目：如果自然的参与被认为至关重要，那么把私权附着于这个新来者就变得困难，但人们对新物品未来行为的信心却很高。所谓“自然”，是给一段漫长故事起的名字；在这段故事中，每一个新事件都受到严格检验，正因如此，它是一个可信的担保者。
反之

，如果这种参与被视为次要的，那么所涉生物体就更容易被据为己有，但认定它完全人工，又使其被动化变得不确定。于是，框定它、控制其行为、监测附带损害，就成为绝对命令；这要求培育出新生物体的人投入大量资源，而此人既然决定尽可能放弃大自然母亲的调节机制，就可能被要求对所产生的影响负责，无论这些影响被评判为好还是坏。当开发者为了给面向市场的被动化提供便利，而同时操纵物品及其关联环境时，后者就构成了一些（暗中）随物品一起出售、却未经任何讨论的世界。在这样的条件下，它们引发争议与抗议，并不令人意外。

Services, given that they increasingly require the involvement of their (human) recipients, also provide a striking illustration of the tensions between passiva(c)tion and appropriation. There are interesting controversies around personal data, the information everyone leaves on networks. Some elements of this data are acquired before the transaction. Other data are produced during the transaction and define, in successive strokes, a taste profile, a profile that is built up as transactions are carried out. Can these data be considered passiva(c)ted goods, and if so, by whom can they be appropriated?
服务日益要求其（人类）接受者参与其中，因此也鲜明地展示了被动化与占有之间的张力。围绕个人数据——每个人留在网络上的信息——存在着有趣的争议。这些数据的一些要素在交易之前就已获得。另一些数据在交易过程中产生，并一次次勾勒出一种品味画像，一种随着交易进行而逐步建立起来的画像。这些数据能否被视为被动化的物品？如果可以，谁又能将它们据为己有？

Consider for a moment to the case of Amazon. The databases the company has built up make it possible to establish that between such and such a date, I had a definite leaning toward a particular type of music, book, or household appliance. Amazon saves the complete series of such data. The data would not exist as a set that could lead to establishing profiles if this recording and saving and the controlled management of its dissemination, with all the costs and necessary technical operations, were not carefully organized. Amazon operates the passiva(c)tion of a part of “me” that, before it was passiva(c)ted by Amazon, did not exist. I bought CDs, books, and household appliances, but these choices were not the focus of any attention. Now that they exist, the data are worked on by Amazon, and they most certainly contribute in a silent, surreptitious way to objectivize me. They appear to have been carefully extracted and separated from me, disentangled from my person in order to give a picture of me. But who can say if this assertion is correct? Nobody. What is for certain is that through Amazon’s computer and commercial strategy, these data start having their own independent life. Then they come back at me on the screen and force me to see in them a sort of reflection of a personality, mine, that had escaped me up until then. It is as if “I” were different from “me.” They seek to give me an image of me, as mirrors are supposed to do, an image I was unable to see by myself that had escaped me up until then. And here is Amazon appropriating these data without even asking me! Granted, these data exist, and certainly exist in a state of passiva(c)tion, only because of Amazon’s operations. Of course, they are not separable from the sociotechnical environment that participates in their elaboration. But this is precisely why, even if they are limited and restricted in this way, the question of the attribution of property rights might arise, and in an acute manner. In the same way that the plant obtained by mutagenesis is unquestionably the result of a close collaboration between nature and its human developers, I would claim that the data by which Amazon defines me and from which it benefits are the fruit of a joint action. And whatever my opinion on the realism and accuracy of these data, I have the right to share in the results. The production and elaboration of these data provide a striking example of a situation in which the goods (data) and their world — what is sometimes called the Amazon fulfillment network and includes my participation and contribution — are simultaneously reconfigured while remaining connected.

且以亚马逊（Amazon）为例稍作考察。该公司建立的数据库使人能够确定：在某两个日期之间，我对某一类音乐、书籍或家用电器有明显偏好。亚马逊保存了这一类数据的完整序列。如果这种记录与保存，以及对其传播的受控管理——连同所有成本和必要的技术操作——没有被精心组织起来，这些数据就不会作为一个能够据以建立画像的集合而存在。亚马逊对“我”的一部分实施了被动化，而这部分在被亚马逊被动化之前并不存在。我买过 CD、书和家用电器，但这些选择从未成为任何关注的焦点。如今它们存在了，这些数据被亚马逊加工，而且它们确实以无声、隐秘的方式把我客体化。它们看起来像是被仔细地从我身上提取并分离出来，从我这个人的身上解缠出来，以便给出一个关于我的图景。但谁能说这一论断是否正确？没有人。可以肯定的是，通过亚马逊的计算机策略与商业策略，这些数据开始拥有自己独立的生活。随后，它们又在屏幕上回到我面前，迫使我从中看到一种人格的映像——我的映像——而这种人格此前一直未被我察觉。就好像“我”（I）不同于“我”（me）。它们试图给我一幅关于我的图像，正如镜子理应做到的那样；这是一幅我自己无法看见、此前一直未被我察觉的图像。而就在这里，亚马逊甚至没有问我一声，就把这些数据据为己有！诚然，这些数据之所以存在，而且确实以一种被动化的状态存在，仅仅是因为亚马逊的操作。当然，它们无法与参与其生成的社会技术环境相分离。但正因如此，即便它们以这种方式被限定和限制，财产权归属的问题仍可能以尖锐的方式提出。正如通过诱变获得的植物无疑是自然与其人类开发者密切协作的结果，我要主张，亚马逊借以界定我、并从中获益的那些数据，是一项联合行动的果实。而无论我对这些数据的真实性与准确性持何种看法，我都有权分享其成果。这些数据的生产与加工，提供了一个鲜明的例子：物品（数据）及其世界——有时被称为亚马逊履约网络（Amazon fulfillment network），其中包括我的参与和贡献——在被同时重新配置的同时，仍保持着连接。

Must I accept that these data be detached from me, reduce me to mere information, when it contributes to building what can be seen by third parties as my identity? In these conditions, it is legitimate that “I” resist this unconsented passiva(c)tion and the reconfiguration it leads to and that “I” claim new rights to be recognized. These are indeed becoming central questions because there are more and more traces that one accounts for and that one takes into account. They are not necessarily limited to simple data extracted from client behavior. Replace Amazon with any biotech company interested in rare diseases and the consumer with any patient suffering from an incurable genetic disease, and you see that the cells he transmits to the company, which will (perhaps) allow the company to design a therapy adapted to his profile, are just as ambivalent as the data Amazon records.

The same problem always comes back, the problem of disentangling, its modalities, and the stakes associated with it. These appear so very problematically in the case of market-oriented passiva(c)tion when the process of detachment and reattachment is oriented toward preparing a market transaction and the transfer of property rights that it requires.

当这些数据参与构建第三方可能视为我的身份的东西时，我是否必须接受它们从我的身上脱离、把我化约为单纯的信息？在这些条件下，“我”抵制这种未经同意的被动化及其导致的重新配置，并要求承认新的权利，是正当的。这些问题确实正变得核心，因为需要交代、需要纳入考虑的痕迹越来越多。它们未必局限于从顾客行为中提取的简单数据。把亚马逊换成任何一家对罕见病感兴趣的生物技术公司，把消费者换成任何一位患有不治遗传病的病人，你就会看到：他传递给公司的细胞——这些细胞（或许）将使公司能够设计出适合其个人情况的疗法——与亚马逊记录的数据一样具有双重性。
同一个问题总是回来：解缠的问题、解缠的方式，以及与之相关的利害。当脱离与再附着的过程指向为市场交易作准备、并指向市场交易所需的财产权转让时，这些问题在面向市场的被动化情形中显得尤为棘手。

The reason I have devoted so many lines to property rights is that in the years to come, they are destined to play a central role in the commoditization process, particularly with the growing importance of so-called intellectual property. Their attribution is a decisive step in the process of passiva(c)tion and can’t be properly understood without the notion of associated milieu that is at the heart of this first framing.
我之所以用这么多篇幅讨论财产权，是因为在未来数年，它们注定要在商品化过程中发挥核心作用，尤其是随着所谓知识产权的日益重要。财产权的归属是被动化过程中的决定性一步；若不借助处于这第一个框定之核心的关联环境概念，就无法恰当理解它。

Before considering the other framings, I would like to demonstrate the fruitfulness of the concept of passiva(c)tion and of its grid of analysis by applying it to a number of goods that have deeply impacted, and still impact, the dynamics of market agencements. These cases will clearly demonstrate how the work of the market-oriented passiva(c)tion of goods functions, the difficulties involved, the trials that have to be overcome, the concerns generated, and the solutions that have to be imagined to assuage them. I am asking for the reader’s patience. The increasingly complex process of the passiva(c)tion of these goods, and in particular, of money, cannot be explained in a few sentences.
在考察其他框定之前，我想把被动化概念及其分析网格应用于若干物品，以此展示其丰产性；这些物品曾深刻影响、并且仍在深刻影响市场装配的动态。这些案例将清楚表明：面向市场的物品被动化工作如何运作，其中涉及哪些困难，必须克服哪些考验，产生了哪些关切，又必须设想哪些解决方案来缓解它们。我请求读者保持耐心。这些物品——尤其是货币——日益复杂的被动化过程，无法用几句话解释清楚。
II. Market-Oriented Passiva(c)tion Is a Never-Ending Odyssey: The Telling Example of Commodities Deemed Fictitious
二、面向市场的被动化是一场永无止境的奥德赛：以被视为虚构的商品为显著例证

Let us recap. Before it can engage in a commercial transaction, a candidate thing, whether an industrial product or a service, must first be disentangled from all those who have engaged in its successive transformations, starting from its conception and including the ways in which it has been marketed. The candidate good will have acquired a quality that can be called (relative) autonomy. This implies that the thing is not condemned to immobility by too great a density of ties. Second, the thing must be capable of acting and making act so that a buyer becomes interested: this is the condition for the candidate to become a commodity, which implies a successful coupling with its associated milieu. The aptitude for entering into courses of action — our third requirement — however, needs to be framed: a market good’s behavior has to be (reasonably) predictable and controllable so as to avoid unexpected and unmanageable disarray. In order for a transfer of property to take place, the good must — fourth condition — have been detached from those who put it into circulation; this can be referred to as the good’s “independence.” Finally, last requirement, it has been made possible to attach property rights to the good and attribute them unambiguously and unobjectionably to a perfectly identifiable Agent A, who is then in a position to cede them to the Buyer B according to prespecified procedures.

让我们先作一回顾。在候选之物——无论是一件工业产品还是一项服务——能够进入商业交易之前，它必须首先从所有参与其一系列相继转化的人那里解缠出来，这些转化从构想阶段开始，也包括将它推向市场的各种方式。候选物品将由此获得一种可以称为（相对）自主性的品质。这意味着，该物不会因关系密度过高而注定静止不动。第二，该物必须能够行动，并能促使他人行动，从而让买方产生兴趣：这是候选者成为商品的条件，而这意味着与其关联环境实现成功的耦合。然而，进入行动过程的能力——我们的第三项要求——需要被框定：市场物品的行为必须是（在合理程度上）可预测、可控制的，以避免意外而难以驾驭的紊乱。为了使财产转移得以发生，物品必须——第四项条件——已从把它投入流通的人那里脱离出来；这可以称为物品的“独立性”。最后，最后一项要求是：已经有可能把财产权附着于物品，并毫无歧义、无可反对地把它们归于一个完全可指认的行动者 A，后者于是能够按照预先规定的程序，把这些权利让渡给买方 B。

Autonomy, the capacity to contribute to courses of action, the predictability of the courses of action elicited, as well as their manageability, and the possibility of attributing property rights to identified agents — these are the main
aptitudes

(or dispositions) with which things must be (gradually) endowed in order for them to acquire the status of commodities. Such faculties are neither natural nor innate. They are all acquired. And that is why one can legitimately speak of market-oriented passiva(c)tion as a task.
自主性、对行动过程作出贡献的能力、所引发的行动过程的可预测性及其可驾驭性，以及把财产权归于已被指认的行动者的可能性——这些就是物为了获得商品身份而必须（逐步）被赋予的主要
能力
（或禀性）。这些能力既非自然天赋，也非与生俱来。它们全都是后天获得的。正因如此，人们才可以正当地把面向市场的被动化称为一项任务。

Although the activities of market-oriented passiva(c)tion are everywhere, they are absent from economics and sociology textbooks. Given how much energy these activities consume, how many questions and problems they raise, this strange silence cannot endure, especially as more living entities enter into the market area and era. Yet although these activities are only now beginning to be seen and analyzed, they are not new. It might be that the history of markets is indistinguishable from the history of the multiple ventures launched throughout the ages in order to passiva(c)te things and bring them into the universe of market activities. In some cases, the difficulties lie in the passiva(c)tion activities themselves and the equilibrium they must reach in order for things to be autonomous and capable of action without being too resistant to control. In other cases, the main problems arise when the detachment of things has to be organized, when property rights have to be associated with them and their alienation made possible. For yet others, what turns out to be particularly hazardous is pulling all the parts of the process together.

尽管面向市场的被动化活动无处不在，它们却在经济学与社会学的教科书中付之阙如。鉴于这些活动耗费多少能量、引发多少问题与难题，这种奇怪的沉默不可能长久维持，尤其随着越来越多的生命体进入市场领域与市场时代。然而，尽管这些活动直到现在才开始被人们看见并加以分析，它们并不新鲜。也许，市场的历史与古往今来为把物被动化、并把它们带入市场活动之宇宙而发起的众多冒险，根本无法区分。在某些情形中，困难在于被动化活动本身，以及这些活动为了物既自主又能够行动、同时又不至于过分抗拒控制而必须达成的平衡。在另一些情形中，主要问题出现在必须组织物的脱离、必须把财产权与物相关联并使物的让渡成为可能之时。而在又一些情形中，尤其危险的是把这一过程的所有部分拼合在一起。

In the following, I will present, albeit in a stylized and perhaps too schematic way, a few of the interminable odysseys through which goods seeking commoditization travel. In this exercise, my aim is not to reach historical truth (that is quite beyond me), but to bring to light the reality and the content of the task of market passiva(c)tion. I will appeal to the grid of analysis presented above to guide this investigation: it will help us understand how to obtain the capacities that determine a thing’s aptitude for transforming into a commodity.
在下文中，我将以程式化、或许过于图式化的方式，呈现若干场无休无止的奥德赛，那些寻求商品化的物品正是经由它们而旅行。在这项练习中，我的目标并不是达到历史真理（那远非我力所能及），而是揭示市场被动化这一任务的现实与内容。我将借助上文提出的分析网格来引导这一考察：它将帮助我们理解，如何获得那些决定一物转化为商品之禀赋的各项能力。

Which cases should I select? From a historical point of view, entities, such as land, work, and money have undoubtedly played and still play a central role in the expansion of market agencements. Many investments, particularly legal ones, were imposed and many battles were fought that led them to a certain kind of (relatively) durable and (relatively) stable passiva(c)tion, which is now irreversible. Let us be clear — retracing this historical process, even in an oversimplified way, is neither endorsing it nor legitimizing it. There is no
one best way
. Evolution, with all its
coups de force
, struggles, and violence, does not mean justice.
我应当选择哪些案例？从历史的角度看，土地、劳动与货币这类实体，无疑曾在、并且仍在市场装配的扩张中扮演核心角色。人们强行推进了许多投入——尤其是法律方面的投入——并经历了许多斗争，它们使这些实体达到某种（相对）持久且（相对）稳定的被动化，而这种被动化如今已不可逆转。我们必须说清楚：回溯这一历史过程，即便以极为简化的方式，既不等于赞同它，也不等于为它辩护。并不存在
唯一的最佳方式
。演化，连同其一切
强力之举
、斗争与暴力，并不意味着正义。

Polanyi, as we know, was particularly interested in these three cases of commodification. He chose them because he had clearly recognized the central role that these goods historically have played in the development and expansion of what he calls the market economy. And it was because he perceived the arbitrary and brutal nature of the commodification of these entities — land, human work, and money — that he invented the notion of fictitious goods. By using the term “fictitious,” which became widely controversial, he most likely wanted to underline that from his point of view, these things were never meant to become commodities and at the same time to claim that current markets are consequently illegitimate and somehow not civilized.

如我们所知，波兰尼对这三个商品化案例特别感兴趣。他选择它们，是因为他清楚地认识到这些物品在所谓市场经济的发展与扩张中历史上所扮演的核心角色。而正是因为他察觉到这些实体——土地、人类劳动与货币——的商品化具有任意而残暴的性质，他才发明了虚构物品（fictitious goods）这一概念。借助“虚构”一词——这个词后来引起广泛争议——他极可能是想强调：从他对事物的看法出发，这些东西从来就不是注定要成为商品的；与此同时，他又想主张：当下的市场因此是不正当的，并且在某种意义上是不文明的。

But how can you decide if a good is fictitious? One answer might be that its commodification process has provoked violent reactions or acts of resistance. One could also imagine, by mobilizing the notion of density, that it cannot be easily dissociated from those who use it, cultivate it, and so on. Both of these criteria would be appropriate, provided, as we will see, that they are considered simultaneously. Yet Polanyi chooses another path, no doubt linked to the industrial economy that surrounds him and to the influence of Marx.
可是，如何判定一件物品是虚构的？一种答案可能是：它的商品化过程引发了激烈的反应或抵抗行动。人们也可以设想，借助密度这一概念，它无法轻易与那些使用它、耕种它等等的人分离开来。这两条标准都会是恰当的，前提是——我们将会看到——它们被同时考虑。然而，波兰尼选择了另一条道路，这无疑与他周围的工业经济以及马克思的影响有关。
According to Polanyi, a commodity is fictitious if it was not produced in order to be sold in the market:
按照波兰尼的说法，一件商品若其生产目的并非在市场出售，那它就是虚构的：

The crucial point is this: labor, land, and money are essential elements of industry; they also must be organized in markets; in fact, these markets form an absolutely vital part of the economic system. But labor, land, and money are obviously not commodities. . . . None of them is produced for sale. The commodity description of labor, land, and money is entirely fictitious. Nevertheless, it is with the help of this fiction that the actual markets for labor, land, and money are organized.
关键之处在于：劳动、土地与货币是工业的基本要素；它们也必须被组织进市场之中；事实上，这些市场构成了经济体系绝对不可或缺的一部分。但劳动、土地与货币显然不是商品。……它们中没有一个是为出售而生产的。把劳动、土地与货币描述为商品，完全是虚构的。然而，正是借助这一虚构，劳动、土地与货币的实际市场才得以组织起来。

Polanyi forgoes all caution when he resorts to the adverb “obviously.” A math teacher I once had frequently told us not to use the word in an oral exam because it inevitably attracts tricky questions from the examiners. Philippe Steiner’s commentary confirms this. He quite rightly observes that by declaring certain commodities fictitious, Polanyi is privileging a particular definition of production, the one that corresponds to the industrial world and its machines.
In market agencements, however, there is no reason for such a restrictive definition.
波兰尼在诉诸“显然”这一副词时，放弃了一切审慎。我从前的一位数学老师常常叮嘱我们，不要在口试中使用这个词，因为它不可避免地会引来考官刁钻的提问。菲利普·施泰纳（Philippe Steiner）的评论证实了这一点。他相当正确地指出：通过宣布某些商品是虚构的，波兰尼实际上偏袒了一种特定的生产定义，即与工业世界及其机器相对应的那种定义。
然而，在市场装配中，没有理由采取如此狭隘的定义。

In order to become a commodity, a thing must go through transformations, enter into the process of passiva(c)tion that accompanies the detaching and reattaching. There is no reason not to consider this very real process as a form of production in its own right. The relevant distinction is not between fiction and reality, but rather between the different gradients of resistance the goods show to passiva(c)tion. From that perspective, but from that perspective alone, Polanyi is not wrong. For the land that turns green in the spring to become a profitable investment; to rent the labor of the human being with whom I speak, exchange, or play and for whom I have affection; for the pocket money I give my children to transform into capital that brings in interest, I will have made many investments and overcome many obstacles!

要成为商品，一物必须经历种种转化，进入伴随脱离与再附着而来的被动化过程。没有理由不把这个极为真实的过程本身视为一种生产。相关的区分不在于虚构与实在之间，而在于物品对被动化所表现出的不同抵抗梯度之间。从这个视角看——但也仅仅从这个视角看——波兰尼并没有错。要让春天变绿的土地成为一项有利可图的投资；要租用那个与我交谈、交换、一同嬉戏、并令我心怀感情的人的劳动；要让我给孩子们的零花钱转化为带来利息的资本，我将不得不作出许多投资，克服许多障碍！

To understand why such efforts have nevertheless been made to turn labor, land, and money into commodities, one need only note what they have in common: they are inexhaustible sources of actions. They suggest actions to which they make a decisive contribution. They are also the potential source of high profits, a common trait that explains their appeal when market agencements are more and more shaped by what is commonly called capitalism.
要理解为何人们仍然付出这般努力，把劳动、土地与货币变成商品，只需注意它们的共同之处：它们是行动的不竭源泉。它们提示出各种行动，并对这些行动作出决定性的贡献。它们也是高额利润的潜在来源，这一共同特征解释了它们的吸引力——尤其当市场装配越来越被通常所谓的资本主义所塑造之时。

For those who strive, for whatever reason, to expand the scope of market transactions, the price to be paid is that the resistance of labor, land, and money to this process of commodification must be overcome. This is not an easy task. Resistance can come from people who oppose this movement and who are helped by the high densities of these entities. Yet frontal confrontation is not the only option. A wide range of strategies have been and could be envisaged, such as attempts to negotiate compromises or to insist that voices raised must be heard. In any case, however, the outcome depends on the dynamics of the power struggles, as discussed in Chapter 8.
对于那些无论出于何种理由都力求扩大市场交易范围的人来说，必须付出的代价是：劳动、土地与货币对这一商品化过程的抵抗必须被克服。这并非易事。抵抗可能来自反对这一运动的人，而这些人又得到这些实体高密度的助力。然而，正面冲突并非唯一选项。人们已经设想、并且还可以设想范围广泛的策略，例如尝试协商妥协，或坚持必须倾听那些发出的声音。不过，无论如何，结果取决于权力斗争的动态，这一点将在第8章讨论。

Human beings have indeed a capacity for creativity and invention that largely surpasses that of all other known entities. They have a great aptitude for acting autonomously. However — and this is the dark side of the force — that aptitude is difficult to discipline, frame, and reduce to behavior that can at least partly be predicted and controlled. Moreover, it cannot be presumed that human beings have an aptitude for being appropriated and alienated.
人类确实拥有一种创造与发明的能力，远远超过所有其他已知实体。他们具有极强的自主行动能力。然而——而这正是力量的阴暗面——这种能力难以被规训、框定，也难以被化约为至少部分可预测、可控制的行为。此外，也不能假定人类具有被占有、被让渡的能力。

Land, or at least some parcels of it, with appropriate, if costly investments, may also hold a huge potential for action: with a bit of construction, it can be lived on; with cultivation, it can nourish those who care for it; with exploration and excavation, it can participate in the production of materials and energy; maintained, it becomes a landscape; properly preserved, it captures greenhouse gases, protects from floods, and filters rain water. Parcels of land are relatively easy to discipline; in other words, they can become predictable. However — and this is their weak spot — they are dense, inclined to immobility, heteronomous, highly dependent on those who participate in the process of its valorization, and consequently resistant, both physically and socially, to alienation.

土地，或者至少其中某些地块，若辅以恰当——尽管代价高昂——的投资，也可能蕴含巨大的行动潜能：稍加建造，就可以在上面居住；加以耕种，它就能滋养照料它的人；通过勘探与挖掘，它可以参与材料与能源的生产；加以维护，它就成为一处景观；妥善保护，它就能捕获温室气体、抵御洪水、过滤雨水。地块相对容易规训；换句话说，它们可以变得可预测。然而——而这正是它们的弱点——它们密度高、倾向于静止、具有他律性，高度依赖参与其价值增殖过程的人，因而在物理上与社会上都抵抗让渡。

As for money, like the living beings to which it is often compared, it is capable of suggesting many courses of action and of participating in them in an independent and autonomous fashion. However, being difficult to master and discipline, it can easily lead to overflowings (
débordements
) and unpredictable catastrophes.
至于货币，就像人们常把它比作的生命体一样，它能够提示许多行动过程，并以独立而自主的方式参与其中。然而，由于难以驾驭和规训，它很容易导致溢出（
débordements
）与不可预测的灾难。

One can already sense that the commodification of human labor, land, and money is no easy task. The high potential for action of these entities is weakened when one attempts to master them or to ensure their autonomy.
人们已经可以感觉到，人类劳动、土地与货币的商品化绝非易事。当人们试图驾驭这些实体、或确保其自主性时，它们那巨大的行动潜能便被削弱了。
HUMAN LABOR
人类劳动

Market agencements are the outcome of long and often violent evolutions that result in whatever configuration they might have at a given time and place. Modalities of passiva(c)tion of goods developed gradually. Multiple forms of arrangements have come to exist, some of which are able to assert their coherence and end up imposing their own temporalities and their own strategic orientations. (See Chapter 7.)
市场装配是漫长而往往暴力的演化的结果，这些演化造就了它们在特定时间与地点可能具有的任何配置。物品被动化的模式逐步发展起来。多种安排形式得以存在，其中一些能够确立自身的融贯性，并最终强加自己的时间性与自身战略取向。（参见第7章。）

The progressive passiva(c)tion of labor is still in progress. Its history is tragic, full of noise and fury, violent actions, backtracking, and ephemeral victories that are quickly contested. Solutions and sociotechnical devices have been devised; some have disappeared, others have survived and spread, establishing compromises between opposing forces and sometimes reaching a balance that is always open to question. So-called human rights and especially social rights have been hard won and must constantly be reclaimed. Without the mobilization of intellectuals, without the ethical questions and the controversies that they have aroused at different times, these inventions and the material, police, and legal measures that accompany them would not have happened. Some of these rights are now widely available. This does not mean that they are the rule.

劳动的渐进被动化仍在进行之中。它的历史是悲剧性的，充满喧嚣与狂怒、暴力行动、倒退，以及很快便受到质疑的短暂胜利。人们设计出了各种解决方案与社会技术装置；其中一些已经消失，另一些则存留下来并扩散开来，在对立力量之间确立妥协，有时达到一种始终可受质疑的平衡。所谓人权、尤其是社会权利，是经过艰苦争取才获得的，并且必须不断被重新争取。若没有知识分子的动员，若没有他们在不同时期激起的伦理问题与争论，这些发明以及伴随它们的物质、警察与法律措施就不会发生。其中一些权利如今已广泛可得。这并不意味着它们已成常规。

In this story, with multiple ramifications, it is possible to pick out at least two crucial stages. What is probably essential in this odyssey is the emergence of slavery, or more precisely, of various types of slavery, in different places and at different times. The statuses of slaves have been indeed highly variable over the course of history. In Rome, for instance, depending on the period, the causes of the enslavement of a human being could be unpaid debt or capture during a war, the slave status of the parents, and so on. In practice, the slave was considered a hybrid being between a thing, which could be sold, and a person to be cared for. He could enjoy variable rights, he could buy back his freedom, exercise professions as different as those of prostitute, secretary, accountant, preceptor, agricultural worker, or even manager of a joint business.

The diversity of his status depended on the state of the balance of power between slaves and free citizens, which included moral rules. (In some cases and at certain times, the master had, for example, the right of life and death over a slave, while in other circumstances, this right was taken away.)

在这段有着多重分支的故事中，至少可以辨认出两个关键阶段。这场奥德赛中或许最根本的，是奴隶制的出现，或者更确切地说，是不同类型奴隶制在不同地点、不同时间的出现。奴隶的地位在历史进程中确实变化极大。例如在罗马，依时期而定，一个人被奴役的原因可能是未偿债务、战争中被俘、父母具有奴隶身份等等。在实践中，奴隶被视为介于可被出售的物与需要照料的人之间的一种混合存在。他可以享有大小不等的权利，可以赎回自由，可以从事各种职业——娼妓、秘书、会计、家庭教师、农业工人，甚至合股企业的管理者。
其地位的多样性取决于奴隶与自由公民之间力量对比的状况，而这种状况也包括道德规则。（例如，在某些情形与某些时期，主人对奴隶拥有生杀之权，而在另一些情况下，这项权利被剥夺。）

Beyond the multifarious forms that slavery takes, it seems plausible that with it, a new possible qualification of the human being emerged, a human being who was put to work and could eventually, at some point, be sold or bought because he could work. Slavery, as one form of harnessing human labor, has not disappeared. As has been well documented, it still exists and even thrives in contemporary societies. Slavery has not faded into the past, even if illegal. When compared with solutions enforced by modern market agencements, it continues to offer an alternative form of the commodification of human work simply because it requires a less demanding associated milieu: a cellar, some Kalashnikovs, the possibility of scaring the person’s family, no constraining regulation, and so on.

撇开奴隶制纷繁多样的形式不谈，看来可以合理推断：随着奴隶制，出现了一种关于人的新的可能品质界定，即一个被投入劳动、并且因为能够劳动而最终可能在某个时刻被出售或买下的人。奴隶制作为役使人类劳动的一种形式，并未消失。正如已有充分记载的那样，它仍然存在，甚至在当代社会中兴盛。奴隶制并未消逝于过去，即便它已属非法。与现代市场装配所推行的解决方案相比，它仍然提供了一种替代性的人类劳动商品化形式，理由很简单：它所需的关联环境要求较低：一间地窖、几支卡拉什尼科夫自动步枪、吓住当事人家人的可能性、没有约束性的规章，等等。

The other stage in the commodification of human labor is the one that led to the notion of a labor force and to the different and evolving devices that allowed this entity to be activated and alienated. Authors such as Marx and Polanyi and the theorists of dispossession such as geographer David Harvey illustrate this long history of the transformation of human labor into a good able to be engaged in a commercial transaction when they underline the historical importance of enclosures, still of contemporary relevance in non-Western countries. These brutal acts are used to detach labor power by ripping it out of its milieu, the world that fosters it, and to transform it into an entity that can be attached to other worlds (for instance that of industrial production) under the condition of monetary compensation (such as a salary).

人类劳动商品化的另一个阶段，导向了劳动力这一概念，以及使这一实体得以被激活、被让渡的各种不同且不断演化的装置。马克思与波兰尼这样的作者，以及地理学家大卫·哈维（David Harvey）这类剥夺理论家，在强调圈地的历史重要性时——圈地在非西方国家至今仍具现实意义——阐明了人类劳动转化为一种能够进入商业交易之物品的这段漫长历史。这些残暴之举被用来把劳动力从其环境中、从养育它的世界中撕扯出来，从而使之脱离，并把它转化为一种可以在金钱补偿（例如工资）的条件下附着于其他世界（例如工业生产的世界）的实体。
Attempts to requalify
human labor
as labor power (which must be produced and, Marx would add, reproduced), requires, as all processes of
commercial passiva(c)tion
do, huge material investments, often accompanied by violent actions. Labor power does not exist outside the devices that frame, format, and “free” it to make it into a commodity.
试图把
人类劳动
重新界定为劳动力（劳动力必须被生产出来，马克思还会补充说，必须被再生产出来），正如一切
商业被动化
过程一样，要求巨大的物质投资，且往往伴随暴力行动。劳动力并不存在于那些框定它、格式化它、并“解放”它使之成为商品的装置之外。

The most intimate human activities have not been spared by this process. For instance, multiple and sophisticated devices have been elaborated over centuries in order to ensure the commercial passiva(c)tion of sexual services: the shop window in Amsterdam erases all attachments — in particular, those that connect the showcased person to family members or the immediate environment. The little red light shows the person to be available for certain courses of action, sometimes explicitly suggested, and at the same time, it ignites desire in some passersby. Nothing can by nature escape market-oriented passiva(c)tion. The success of the process depends on the capacity of some agents to impose their own strategic visions. This capacity hinges on whatever contributes to ensuring a leading role in enacting adequate socio-technical devices: law, police, or military interventions, machine design, management rules, expert knowledge, monetary resources, moral principles, religious prescriptions, the whole being seasoned with a grain of trickery and Machiavellianism. Anything goes if no one can oppose.

最私密的人类活动也未能幸免于这一过程。例如，数百年来，人们设计出多种多样而精巧的装置，以确保性服务的商业被动化：阿姆斯特丹的橱窗抹去了一切附着——尤其是那些把被展示者与家庭成员或周遭环境联系起来的附着。那盏小红灯表明此人可供某些行动过程使用——这些行动过程有时被明确提示——与此同时，它也在某些路人心中点燃欲望。没有任何东西在本质上能逃脱面向市场的被动化。这一过程的成功，取决于某些行动者强加自身战略视野的能力。这种能力取决于一切有助于确保在制定适当的社会技术装置中占据主导地位的东西：法律、警察或军事干预、机器设计、管理规则、专家知识、货币资源、道德原则、宗教规定，而这一切还要加上一撮欺诈与马基雅维利主义。只要无人能够反对，什么都可以。

From a descriptive standpoint, why should we insist on maintaining that labor power is a commodity distinct from all the others? Granted, it has certain particular characteristics, but nothing prevents it from being transformed into a commodity: although the particular difficulties may change in this case, the general process for achieving commodification does not. It involves producing, via successive transformations, framed autonomy and transferable entities (the service rendered), detaching in order to reattach. The human being is translated into work and the work into labor power. The service delivered can then be attributed to the latter and paid to the person who provides it. This requalification, which was in no way self-evident, now takes place as a matter of routine and on a large scale. By framing it in words shared with physics (“work,” “power”), this qualification designates and enacts an entity that acts, and makes act and react, which must be kept up (trained), maintained, and framed by a set of devices that are material (machines, for example), institutional (hierarchy, for example), or textual (labor law, for example). The human being is “domesticated” and transformed. This domestication through successive requalifications is never completed. The design of devices that frame, orient, and mobilize labor power constantly evolve as an outcome of shifting power relationships and trials of strength.

从描述的角度看，我们为何要坚持主张劳动力是一种与其他一切商品都不同的商品？诚然，它具有某些特殊特征，但没有什么阻止它转化为商品：尽管在此情形中具体困难会有所变化，实现商品化的一般过程并不改变。它涉及通过一系列相继转化，生产出被框定的自主性与可转移的实体（所提供的服务），涉及先脱离以便再附着。人被转译为劳动，劳动又被转译为劳动力。所提供的服务于是可以归于后者，其报酬则支付给提供服务的人。这种重新界定品质绝非不言自明，如今却作为例行之事大规模地发生。通过用与物理学共享的词语（work、power）来框定它，这种品质界定指认并施行了一个行动着、并促使他者行动和作出反应的实体；这个实体必须由一整套装置来维持（训练）、保养和框定，这些装置是物质的（例如机器）、制度的（例如等级制）或文本的（例如劳动法）。人被“驯化”并转化。这种通过反复重新界定品质而实现的驯化，从未完成。框定、引导并动员劳动力的装置设计，作为不断变动的权力关系与力量考验的结果，持续演化。

In his study of the French textile industry in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, William Reddy describes the controversial process that, through successive stages, led industrial employers to manage work as a commodity. There were no self-evident answers to the questions they asked themselves. What does the entrepreneur buy? How can work be measured? The answers were imagined and imposed over time. There was no dearth of conflicts and struggles. Little by little, however, workers were forced to accept that their compensation would be linked to the variable effort they put in and that this would be measured by attributing a monetary value to the movement of a finger or the length of a lunch break.

Yves-Marie Abraham has shown how, since 1848, when the border between Mexico and the United States was drawn as it is today, Mexican labor has been progressively and enduringly domesticated by American firms.
First the workers were imported, reduced to a purely muscular labor force, cut off(disentangled and detached) from their home milieus, parked in uncomfortable camps; the
braceros
(those equated with mere arms) were easily commoditized. The second stage was that of the
maquiladoras

, American firms crossing the border in order to continue to take advantage of a workforce formatted as it was in the first period, but now courtesy of the Mexican state. Then came the time of illegal migration and workers without papers, a very efficient device for maintaining the earlier frameworks for managing the workforce, this time through the fear of being sent back to Mexico. The author’s conclusion is beyond dispute. Despite an array of objections for moral reasons, convictions about equality, or simply human empathy, in the absence of interventions to stop the processes that produce it, human labor is not a fictitious commodity: appropriately formatted, it is a fullfledged commodity, very real, and very concrete.

威廉·雷迪（William Reddy）在对18、19世纪法国纺织业的研究中，描述了那个充满争议的过程：它经过若干相继阶段，使工业雇主把劳动当作商品来管理。他们向自己提出的问题并没有不言自明的答案。企业家买的究竟是什么？劳动如何能被计量？这些答案是被想象出来、并随时间被强加的。冲突与斗争从不缺乏。然而，工人们一点一点被迫接受：他们的报酬将与他们投入的可变努力相挂钩，而这种努力将通过给一个手指的动作或午休时间的长短赋予货币价值来计量。
伊夫-玛丽·亚伯拉罕（Yves-Marie Abraham）表明，自1848年墨西哥与美国之间的边界被划定成今天这个样子以来，墨西哥劳动如何被美国企业逐步而持久地驯化。
首先是输入工人，把他们化约为纯粹肌肉的劳动力，使他们与其家乡环境切断（解缠并脱离），把他们安置在简陋的营地里；这些“臂膀工”（
braceros
，即被等同于单纯臂膀的人）很容易被商品化。第二个阶段是出口加工厂（
maquiladoras

）阶段：美国企业越过边界，以便继续利用按第一阶段方式格式化好的劳动力，只不过这一次是借墨西哥国家之力。随后到来的是非法移民与无证工人的时代——这是一种维持早先劳动力管理框架的极为有效的装置，这一次靠的是被遣返墨西哥的恐惧。作者的结论无可争议。尽管有出于道德理由的反对、关于平等的信念，或仅仅是人的同情，在缺乏干预以阻止产生它的那些过程的情况下，人类劳动并非虚构商品：经过恰当格式化，它是一种十足的商品，非常真实，也非常具体。

Taylorization and the ways of shaping the workforce it imposed are an important chapter in this story. Laurent Thévenot provides us with a precise description of the range of activities, the technologies and knowledge, required to develop and produce the machinery that ensures both the autonomy of the workforce and its management. As he explains, “Taylor’s handbook, therefore, contains a particularly large repertoire of form-giving instruments. . . . In it are to be found objects used in production on the shop floor, instruments, plans, conventions, scientific formulas, school precepts, ways of giving instructions which are close to military orders, methods of payment to be used in companies, principles, advice and examples to follow when deciding what action to take.”

泰勒制（Taylorization）以及它所强加的塑造劳动力的方式，是这段故事中重要的一章。洛朗·泰弗诺（Laurent Thévenot）为我们精确描述了开发与生产这样一套机器所需的活动范围、技术与知识，这套机器既确保劳动力的自主性，又确保对它的管理。正如他所解释的：“因此，泰勒的手册包含了一份特别庞大的赋形工具清单。……在其中可以找到车间生产中使用的物件、工具、图纸、惯例、科学公式、学校训诫、近乎军事命令的下达指令方式、公司中使用的付酬方法、原则、建议，以及在决定采取何种行动时可资遵循的范例。”

These formatting operations, both difficult and costly, are often associated with production imperatives. We do not consider them to belong to market activity itself, whereas in fact they are situated at the very heart of it insofar as they facilitate the attribution and transfer of property rights. As one could expect, the planned economies of Eastern Bloc countries, when they were trying to directly quantify the labor value to measure the exchange value of goods, participated in this venture, the market passiva(c)tion of human labor. They contributed to conceiving precise ways of measuring the different elements of the work process. This led, in the end, to the concept of a unit of work, making it possible to evaluate workers’ productivity and to distribute revenues according to this measure. Martha Lampland, who reconstituted the history of these practices and devices from the 1920s to the 1950s in Hungary, shows that these experiences played a part, without it ever being avowed, in the development of a science of human labor commoditization.

这些格式化操作既困难又昂贵，往往与生产上的必要要求相关联。我们并不认为它们属于市场活动本身，而事实上，它们恰恰处于市场活动的核心，因为它们为财产权的归属与转让提供了便利。不出所料，东欧集团国家的计划经济在试图直接量化劳动价值、以衡量商品交换价值时，也参与了这一事业，即人类劳动的市场被动化。它们参与构想精确的方法，以计量劳动过程的不同要素。这最终导致了劳动单位（unit of work）这一概念，使人们能够评估工人的生产率，并依此分配收入。玛莎·兰普兰（Martha Lampland）重构了20世纪20年代至50年代匈牙利这些实践与装置的历史，她表明，这些经验在从未被公开承认的情况下，参与了人类劳动商品化科学的形成。

Taylorization of the workforce establishes a compromise between the diverse requirements for market passiva(c)tion, a compromise that privileges the need to domesticate labor and operates to the detriment of the human aptitude for starting new courses of action. To respond to the criticism leveled against Taylorization and to move beyond its limits, industry invented new forms of organization that Luc Boltanski and Ève Chiapello have gathered under the suggestive rubric of the “new spirit of capitalism.” These transformations, which it would be wrong to mistake for a simple process of work intensification, shift the point of equilibrium between, on the one hand, framing the workforce in such a way that it accomplishes certain (measurable) actions and, on the other hand, framing the workforce as a source of novel courses of action — that is, between the workforce that
does
and the workforce that
invents
. The passiva(c)tion process, by its very nature, is always torn between two contradictory requirements.

Organizing by “project groups,” a mantra for experts in industrial organization, marks a new point of equilibrium between autonomy, initiative, and management and augurs new forms of resistance, overflowings that will in turn have to be taken into account by passiva(c)tion devices.

劳动力的泰勒制在市场被动化的各项不同要求之间确立了一种妥协，这种妥协偏重驯化劳动的需要，而有损于人类开启新行动过程的能力。为了回应针对泰勒制的批评并超越其局限，工业界发明了新的组织形式，吕克·博尔坦斯基（Luc Boltanski）与伊芙·夏皮罗（Ève Chiapello）把这些形式汇集在“资本主义新精神”这一富于暗示的标题之下。这些转变——若把它们误认为单纯的劳动强化过程，那就错了——移动了平衡点：一边是把劳动力框定为完成某些（可计量的）行动的东西，另一边是把劳动力框定为新颖行动过程的源泉，也就是在
实做
的劳动力与
发明
的劳动力之间移动平衡点。被动化过程依其本性，总是在两项相互矛盾的要求之间被撕扯。
按“项目团队”来组织——这是工业组织专家的一句口头禅——标志着在自主性、主动性与管理之间达到新的平衡点，并预示着新的抵抗形式，即那些反过来又必须被被动化装置纳入考虑的溢出。

Like any entity shaped to be passiva(c)ted, labor power requires an associated milieu that makes possible, promotes, and frames the enactment of its capacity to act. For each configuration, it would be quite easy to make a detailed inventory of these assemblages. The sociotechnical organization of work, law, unemployment, vocational training, educational system, infrastructures allowing mobility and transfer, are nothing but an indicative list of those elements.
如同任何被塑造以便被被动化的实体一样，劳动力需要一个关联环境，来使其行动能力的施行成为可能、得到促进并被框定。对于每一种配置，都不难为这些装配列出详细清单。劳动的社会技术组织、法律、失业、职业培训、教育体系、使流动与转移得以实现的基础设施，都只是这些要素的一份指示性清单。
LAND
土地

The same analysis would allow us to follow the transformations and the requalifications of land, to trace the main stages of its commercial passiva(c)tion over the long term. It would become clear that a number of episodes, such as the advent of enclosures, are shared with the history of human labor and of labor power. Land’s weak point is not its propensity to reject all forms of discipline: on the contrary, unfortunately, it tends to withstand the worst hardship in silence. Its weakness, rather, is its limited capacity for autonomy. Land does not move; it cannot be moved.
同样的分析可以让我们追踪土地的转化与品质的重新界定，追溯其商业被动化在长时段中的主要阶段。这样一来就会清楚：若干插曲——例如圈地运动的兴起——与人类劳动和劳动力（labor power）的历史是共有的。土地的弱点并不在于它倾向于拒绝一切形式的规训：恰恰相反，不幸的是，它往往默默承受最恶劣的磨难。它的弱点毋宁说在于其自主能力有限。土地不会移动；它无法被移动。

However, no battle is impossible to win. Just as some human beings were transformed willy-nilly into labor power, land has gradually become documents in the form of sheets of paper, light and easy to set into motion, that constitute property rights that are easy to attribute and easy to commute. There is nothing original or extraordinary about the procedure required to produce land commodities. Land is closed, confined, registered, transformed into plots on a map, qualified as a constructible zone, or agricultural land, or as participating in a space devoted to promising economic development. It can be the object of notarized deeds; it can be transferred, sold. With these new qualities, produced in a novel form, it becomes an entity that can engage in commercial transactions: it circulates from hand to hand, suggesting courses of action whose variety increases in proportion to the abundance of available qualifications. The devices that allow for it to be made into a commodity are as complex as, but no more fictitious than those that transform the human being into labor power or a merino sheep into lamb chops in a supermarket. This is no longer the same land, and yet it is still that land. Note, however, that the mechanisms operating here can be found everywhere; they aim at detaching an entity, translating and transforming it, stabilizing it and making it active — in short, at making it available for courses of action that it suggests and in which it participates.

然而，没有哪一场战斗是不可能打赢的。正如一些人类存在者被不由分说地转化为劳动力，土地也渐渐变成了以纸张形式存在的文件——轻便、便于移动，构成易于归属、也易于转换的财产权。生产土地商品所需的程序并无任何原创或非凡之处。土地被围合、被限定、被登记，被转化为地图上的地块，被界定为可建设区、农业用地，或被界定为参与某个有望带来经济发展的空间。它可以成为公证文书的标的；它可以被转让、被出售。凭借这些以新颖形式生产出来的新品质，它成为一个能够参与商业交易的实体：它从一只手传到另一只手，提示出各种行动方案，而这些方案的多样性随可用品质界定的丰富程度而增加。使土地得以成为商品的装置，与那些把人类存在者转化为劳动力、或把一头美利奴羊（merino sheep）转化为超市里的羊排的装置同样复杂，但并不比它们更为虚构。这不再是同一块土地，然而它仍然是那块土地。不过请注意，此处运作的机制随处可见；它们旨在使一个实体脱离、转译并转化它、稳定它并使之活跃——简言之，使它可供它所提示、并参与其中的行动方案使用。

Once it has been requalified by these passiva(c)tion devices, land, just like the human being, is different, and yet is still present as land. The metaphor that comes to my mind is transubstantiation, so well glossed in Luis Buñuel’s
The Milky Way

. The rabbit is (indeed) in the rabbit pâté, but in a different form from the rabbit running in the fields; the fish is in the fish stick, but in a different form from what it is in the wild, in the depths of the ocean. Would one say of the rabbit in the pâté that it is more fictitious than the one in the fields? Would one say of the cod that I unfreeze in the microwave that it is more fictitious than the one Norwegian fishermen pull up off the coast of Newfoundland? Obviously not! The same goes for the two lands, the one in the land registry and the one that feeds the wild boar. Considered at different stages of the qualification and passiva(c)tion process, they are as fictitious and as real as one another. The material operations of translation and production that transform and displace can obviously be contested, and indeed are contested in much the same terms. This fish stick is awful! This pâté has no taste! The land described by this vile piece of paper, which the notary reads with a shaking voice in front of buyers who are total strangers to me, has nothing to do with the land that my ancestors handed down to me! The labor power you buy at slashed prices is an offense to human beings and their dignity! One would have to be deaf not to hear them and incredibly naïve to think that these denunciations or criticisms are enough to threaten the course of market passiva(c)tion.
土地一旦经由这些被动化装置重新界定品质，就像人类存在者一样，既已不同，又仍然作为土地在场。我想到的隐喻是“实体转变”（transubstantiation），路易斯·布努埃尔（Luis Buñuel）在《银河》（
The Milky Way

）中对它作了精彩的诠释。兔子（确实）在兔肉酱里，但形态不同于田野里奔跑的兔子；鱼在鱼柳条里，但形态不同于它在海洋深处野生状态中的样子。人们会说肉酱里的兔子比田野里的兔子更虚构吗？人们会说我放进微波炉解冻的鳕鱼，比挪威渔民在纽芬兰（Newfoundland）外海捕上来的鳕鱼更虚构吗？显然不会！这两块土地也是如此：一块在地籍簿里，一块喂养野猪。从品质界定与被动化过程的不同阶段来看，它们彼此同样虚构，也同样真实。那些进行转化与位移的转译和生产之物质操作，显然可以被质疑，而且也确实以大体相同的措辞受到质疑。这条鱼柳真难吃！这肉酱毫无味道！这张卑劣的纸所描述的土地——公证人在那些与我完全陌生的买主面前用颤抖的声音宣读它——与我祖先传给我的那块土地毫无关系！你以跳楼价买来的劳动力，是对人类及其尊严的侮辱！人除非聋了才听不见这些声音；而若以为这些谴责或批评足以威胁市场被动化的进程，那就天真得难以置信。
MONEY AND ITS DERIVATIVES
货币及其衍生品

Money, the third element of Polanyi’s triptych of fictitious commodities, deserves particular attention. First, because its increasing commodification, corresponding to what is usually referred to as the financialization of the economy, has an expanding impact on people’s lives and in particular on the growth of social inequalities.

Second, because analyzing the modalities of its market passiva(c)tion sheds interesting light on the subtle mechanisms of this general process. In this introduction to these matters, I do not mean to undertake the
n
th history or genealogy of money.

Instead, I aim to highlight that it constantly fluctuates between two modes of existence, that of a strictly framed and profiled technical instrument that enters into clearly defined and controlled courses of action and that of an entity that, even as it accomplishes the functions specified for it, can, as it passes from hand to hand, provoke new courses of action that are hard to control, stoking dreams of riches and power, inflaming speculation, nourishing behavior oriented by greed or — perhaps more rarely — altruism. The case of money is all the more interesting to consider because the problem of finding a balance between the order it allows for and the disorders it produces has been at the heart of incessant debates, so great is its capacity for activating passions.
货币是波兰尼（Karl Polanyi）虚构商品三联体中的第三项，值得特别关注。首先，因为其日益加深的商品化——通常所谓的经济金融化——对人们的生活、尤其是对社会不平等的加剧，产生着不断扩大的影响。
其次，因为分析其市场被动化的诸种样态，能为这一总体过程的微妙机制提供有趣的启示。在这段引论中，我无意撰写第
n
部货币史或货币谱系学。

我更想强调：货币不断在两种存在方式之间摆动——一种是严格框定、经过品质塑造的技术工具，进入界定明确且受控制的行动方案；另一种则是一个实体，即便在履行指定给它的功能时，也能在从一只手传到另一只手的过程中激发新的、难以控制的行动方案，点燃对财富与权力的梦想，煽动投机，滋养由贪婪驱动、或——也许更罕见地——由利他之心驱动的行为。货币的情形尤其值得考察，因为如何在它所容许的秩序与它所制造的失序之间找到平衡，一直是连绵不绝的争论的核心，它激活激情的能力如此之大。

Money’s passiva(c)tion process is an amazing story. Each new move raises deep concerns and fuels heated debates and violent struggles. It acts as a magnifying lens making visible the trials any entity has to pass on the way to commoditization. Yet this particular angle of view has been overlooked. The issues that usually get discussed revolve around oppositions seen as structural, such as the one between token and material stuff or between state money and market money.

Others focus their analysis on the diversity of monies and their institutional hierarchies. By considering its commoditization/passiva(c)tion process, we get rid of these usual binarisms and classifications.
货币的被动化过程是一段惊人的故事。每一次新的推进都会引发深切忧虑，助长激烈辩论与暴力斗争。它像一面放大镜，使任何实体在通往商品化之路上必须经受的考验变得可见。然而，这一特定视角一直遭到忽视。通常被讨论的问题，围绕着被视为结构性的对立展开，例如符号凭证（token）与物质材料之间的对立，或国家货币与市场货币之间的对立。
另一些研究则把分析集中于货币的多样性与制度等级。通过考察其商品化/被动化过程，我们可以摆脱这些惯常的二元对立与分类。
Before starting, I should emphasize that considering the process of the market passiva(c)tion of money as an object of study per se is the complete inverse from theses that assert that money
is

a commodity. For example, as it will be easy to notice, my analysis of money as commodity departs from the opposite assumptions of the Marxian tradition. For me, money becomes a commodity not because of something that would be its inherent value (such as labor value), but because it can be transformed into what is usually called credit, its price being the interest paid by the buyer to the seller. As I will document further, this requalification is the founding step in a long series of derivations that deepen and extend its never-ending commoditization process. To have an overall and updated view of this process, it will thus be necessary to pay particular attention to most recent and sophisticated financial products.
开始之前，我应强调：把货币的市场被动化过程本身当作研究对象，与那些断言货币
就是

商品的论点完全相反。例如，人们很容易注意到，我把货币作为商品来分析时，所依据的假设与马克思主义传统恰好相反。在我看来，货币成为商品，并不是因为某种可称为其内在价值的东西（例如劳动价值），而是因为它能被转化为通常所谓的信用，其价格就是买方向卖方支付的利息。正如我将在后文详加说明的，这一重新界定品质，是一长串衍生（derivations）的奠基性步骤，这些衍生不断加深并扩展其永无止境的商品化过程。因此，要获得对这一过程的总体而最新的看法，就必须特别关注最新、最复杂的金融产品。

Let us start with the obvious. No entity is destined by its essence to play the role of what anthropologists (or economists) usually consider money. An indirect proof of this is given by the variety of things, materials, or objects that in different societies and different eras have been used: dolphin teeth, gold or silver coins, seashells, cigarettes, stamps, paper bills, and so on. And this diversity is increasing, rather than decreasing. When I go shopping, I carry in my bag coins, bills, my checkbook, my credit or debit cards, and also my mobile phone transformed into a means of payment; when I went for a walk in Rome in the 1970s, I always took with me stamps or sweets to sweeten the deal of any transaction. The list is endless.

从显而易见的说起。没有任何实体因其本质而注定扮演人类学家（或经济学家）通常所谓的货币角色。一个间接证据是：在不同社会与不同时代，被使用过的事物、材料或物件种类繁多：海豚牙齿、金银币、贝壳、香烟、邮票、纸币，等等。而且这种多样性在增加，而非减少。我去购物时，包里装着硬币、纸币、支票簿、信用卡或借记卡，还有被改造成支付手段的手机；20世纪70年代我在罗马散步时，总随身带着邮票或糖果，以便给任何交易加点甜头。这份清单无穷无尽。
Rather than defining money through its supposed characteristics, it is tempting, as has been the custom since Aristotle, to define it through the functions it fulfills.
不通过货币被假定的特征，而像亚里士多德以来的惯例那样，通过它所履行的功能来定义货币，是一种很有吸引力的做法。
Four functions are generally recognized. First, money serves as a
means of payment

. It makes it possible to acquire a good and conclude the transfer of property rights. When I buy a bottle of olive oil at the supermarket, I pay for the right to put it in my shopping bag. As an ordinary economic agent, what I am experiencing is that money allows me to settle my purchases. The cashier thinks in the same terms when asking whether I will pay in cash, or by card, or by check. In a few seconds, I take on a debt, which I will pay off, either immediately if I pay cash or later if I use a Visa card. Likewise, when I pay back a mortgage, I make payments according to a schedule that has set the amounts and the timetable.
通常承认四种功能。第一，货币作为
支付手段
。它使人们能够取得一件物品并完成财产权转移。当我在超市买一瓶橄榄油时，我支付的是把它放进购物袋的权利。作为一个普通经济行动者，我所体验到的是：货币让我结清购物款。收银员问我是付现金、刷卡还是支票时，想的也是同一回事。几秒钟内，我承担了一笔债务，随后将其清偿：若付现金便立即清偿，若用维萨卡（Visa）则稍后清偿。同样，当我偿还按揭时，我按照一份规定了金额与时间表的计划付款。
The second function usually ascribed to money is that of a
medium

that facilitates exchanges. It is said that without money, human beings would have to engage in complicated barter operations in order to obtain the necessities of life. If I need eggs, ham, pickles, and bread to make a sandwich, and money does not exist, I will be forced to find the people who have these ingredients or who are willing to procure them for me in exchange for the goods and services I possess. If everyone had to proceed in this way, the task would rapidly become very complex, and everyone would spend their time trying to find a partner willing to accept the exchange they seek. Money, or so the thinking goes, avoids these complications: as long as I am rich enough, I can acquire everything I need in a single visit to the neighborhood supermarket. It is a sort of lubricant that makes transactions in a complex society easier; it is a substitute for bartering,
which, on the contrary, would impede these transactions.
通常赋予货币的第二种功能，是作为便利交换的
媒介

。据说，若没有货币，人类为了获得生活必需品，就不得不进行复杂的物物交换。如果我需要鸡蛋、火腿、腌黄瓜和面包来做三明治，而货币不存在，我就得去找拥有这些食材、或愿意为我弄来这些食材、以换取我手中物品与服务的人。如果人人都得这样做，事情很快就会变得极其复杂，人人都会把时间花在寻找愿意接受其所求交换的伙伴上。据称，货币避免了这些麻烦：只要我足够有钱，就能去一趟社区超市买齐所需的一切。它是一种润滑剂，使复杂社会中的交易更容易；它是物物交换的替代品，
而物物交换反倒会阻碍这些交易。

Despite the almost unanimous support for this way of understanding its function, its reality is far from obvious. Who actually goes through the checkout considering they are exchanging banknotes for leeks? The function of money as a means of exchange emerges only in exceptional circumstances, and even there, it operates in the opposite way from what is expected. Many authors in fact consider, with good reason, that barter does not precede money, but rather substitutes for it in case of need, and that it appeared, and is likely to appear, only after money did.

Barter takes over when money is missing or when it is incapable of fulfilling its other functions properly. The inverse is implausible because exchange, even in a simple form, requires cognitive skills well beyond human faculties. Exchange without money is possible only in particular situations where an existing currency is missing or creates more problems than it solves. In this case, the agents can rely on it mentally to carry out their calculations. It is in reference to these current situations that we can speak of money as a means of exchange: it is money that allows barter, and not barter that, because of its failures, paves the way for the emergence of money. In other situations, it seems better to stick to the first function, that of means of payment.
尽管这种理解货币功能的方式几乎得到一致支持，其现实性却远非显而易见。有谁在收银台前会觉得自己是在用纸币换韭葱呢？货币作为交换手段的功能，只在例外情形中才显现，而且即便在那里，其运作方式也与预期相反。事实上，许多作者有充分理由认为，物物交换并不先于货币，而是在需要时取代货币；它是在货币出现之后才出现、并且很可能还会出现的。

当货币缺失、或无法恰当履行其他功能时，物物交换便接手。相反的情形难以成立，因为交换即便采取简单形式，所需的认知能力也远超人类官能。没有货币的交换，只在特定情境中才可能：此时一种现行货币缺失，或它造成的问题多于它所解决的问题。在这种情况下，行动者可以在心智上依靠它进行计算。正是参照这些当前情境，我们才能说货币是交换手段：是货币使物物交换成为可能，而不是物物交换因其失败而为货币的出现铺平道路。在其他情境中，似乎最好坚持第一种功能，即支付手段。
The third function usually attributed to money is that it can be used as a
store of value

. If I raise chickens and sell them at the end of the month for more than I need for my regular consumption, I can keep my gains in the form of money, which I will use later for new purchases. In this case, money acts as an asset that transports purchasing power from one period to another and/or from one point in space to another. For it to be able to play this role, it must be the case that in this other point of space-time, it maintains its function as a payment instrument.
通常赋予货币的第三种功能，是它可以充当
价值贮藏手段
。如果我养鸡，并在月底把鸡卖掉，所得超过日常消费所需，我就可以把收益以货币形式保存起来，日后用于新的购买。在此情形中，货币充当一种资产，把购买力从一时段运送到另一时段，和/或从空间中的一点运送到另一点。要让它扮演这一角色，就必须满足一个条件：在另一个时空点上，它仍保持其支付工具的功能。
Finally, in the fourth function usually mentioned, money is used as an
accounting unit

, providing a convenient and coherent means of affixing prices and hence of comparing the values of different goods that it makes commensurable. Instead of saying (as in a fictional system without money) that a pineapple is worth six pots of yogurt, which in turn are worth four liters of milk, I can say that their price is the same — seven euros — and I can begin complicated arithmetical operations.
最后，在通常提到的第四种功能中，货币被用作
记账单位
，提供便利而连贯的手段来标定价格，从而比较不同物品的价值，使它们可以通约。与其说（如同在一个没有货币的虚构体系中）一只菠萝值六罐酸奶，而六罐酸奶又值四升牛奶，我可以说它们的价格相同——七欧元——于是便能开始复杂的算术运算。

Is it satisfying to stick to this instrumental definition of money and to the list of the four functions it fulfills? The answer is no. First, because the functions that make something into money in the usual sense given to this word have a history; they are not given once and for all; they constantly evolve.

Furthermore, and more importantly, this general (and purely instrumental) definition of money and its functions is not satisfactory because in reality, the properties that allow these functions to be performed exert irrepressible pressure on it to transform it, at a stroke, into a financial product, into a good that can be bought and sold against payment. A rapid detour to examine the qualities required for it to fulfill its different functions will make this point clearer.
满足于这种对货币的工具性定义、满足于它所履行的四项功能清单，是否令人满意？答案是否定的。首先，因为使某物成为通常所谓货币的那些功能有其历史；它们并非一劳永逸地给定，而是不断演化。
此外，更重要的是，这种对货币及其功能的一般（且纯属工具性的）定义并不令人满意，因为在现实中，使这些功能得以履行的属性会对货币施加不可抑制的压力，使它一举转化为一种金融产品，一种可以买卖、以支付为对价的物品。快速绕道考察一下货币履行不同功能所需的品质，会使这一点更清楚。

Precious metals were often chosen to serve as money because of their material aptitude for accomplishing certain instrumental tasks.
