Having been extracted from the earth, duly transformed and conditioned, they are able to withstand the handovers and long circuits that commercial transactions sometimes require, and therefore they constitute an efficient means of exchange. In the form of coins, they can be added or divided, which makes them good candidates for the functions of accounting units and means of payment. Being resistant to corrosion and to the passage of time, they can be accumulated and stocked. Their purity can be controlled, and their properties are easily guaranteed. These properties prepare them to be used to store value. Granted, they have certain defects: they are unwieldy and heavy, specific equipment is required to measure their weight and control their composition, but all in all, they constitute loyal instruments.

贵金属常被选作货币，是因为其物质属性适合完成某些工具性任务。它们从地下开采出来，经过适当转化与加工，能够承受商业交易有时所需的多次转手与漫长流转，因而是高效的交换手段。以硬币形式，它们可以被加总或分割，这使它们成为记账单位与支付手段功能的良好候选者。它们耐腐蚀、抗时间侵蚀，可以被积累和储存。其纯度可以控制，其属性容易担保。这些属性使它们适于充当价值贮藏。诚然，它们有某些缺陷：笨重、不便携带，需要专门设备来称重并检验成分，但总体而言，它们是忠实的工具。

The material characteristics that authorize the successful accomplishment of their instrumental functions as money facilitate the transformation of precious metals into commodities. This is the case, first because they provide material for manufacturing things such as utensils or jewelry.
Anthropologists and economists are right to speak of “commodity money” when they refer to these types of money, which are easy to pass(act)ivate and to convert.
使贵金属得以成功履行其货币工具功能的物质特征，也便利了它们转化为商品。这首先是因为它们为制造器皿或首饰之类的东西提供了材料。
人类学家和经济学家在指称这类货币时，说“商品货币”（commodity money）是正确的——这类货币容易被动化—激活，也容易转换。

However, the aptitude of money to transform itself or to be transformed into a commodity is not limited to such simple recycling operations. If I have a hundred-gram piece of gold (accounting unit), I can choose to preserve it (store of value) and use it later as a means of payment that will allow me to acquire an “exchangeable” good (means of exchange) for this coin. I can also, however, be convinced to lend it to someone who is short on means of payment in return for an additional sum. I make my hundred grams of gold available to him, and he buys the use of it at a certain price, corresponding to what is called interest. The coin thereby acquires commodity status, not because it is gold, but because it has stable functions that interest my buyer: he will be able to mobilize it for specific courses of action (to buy a car, hoarding, or whatever). It has become an asset, or what in French bears the felicitous name “
un actif
.” In this case, this asset is described as financial. The money (my gold coin) generates money (the interest paid by the borrower).

然而，货币转化为商品、或被转化为商品的能力，并不限于这类简单的回收利用操作。如果我有一块一百克的金子（记账单位），我可以选择保存它（价值贮藏），日后把它用作支付手段，用以购得一件“可交换的”物品（交换手段）。但我也可以被说服把它借给某个缺少支付手段的人，以换取一笔额外的款项。我把这一百克金子交给他使用，他则以一定价格购买其使用权，这个价格就是所谓的利息。于是这枚金币获得了商品地位，不是因为它由黄金制成，而是因为它具有我的买主所感兴趣的稳定功能：他将能够为特定行动方案（买车、囤积，或别的什么）调动它。它变成了一项资产，或者说，在法语中有一个恰如其分的名称——“
un actif
”（资产）。在此情形中，这项资产被描述为金融资产。货币（我的金币）生出货币（借款人支付的利息）。
In order for this strange generation to take place, the money must have a new quality that is suggestively called “liquidity.”

Liquidity (greater or smaller: there are “degrees of liquidity”) measures its (greater or lesser) capacity to maintain and have a good chance of successfully accomplishing its functions. If the money (candidate for commodity status) could not be used as a means of payment at some later date and in some other place, if its value were not preserved, I doubt that my borrower would accept to shell out money (the interest he will pay me) to have the right to use it. Money, through its functions, allows certain actions (buying, selling, hoarding, and so on) to be accomplished. For it to transform into a commodity, it is necessary and sufficient that the capacity to undertake these actions be guaranteed over time and through space. It is not therefore fundamentally different from the Volkswagen Golf we were considering earlier. Just like the car, the money needs an associated milieu that makes its uses possible. To move about, the Golf requires, among other things, road infrastructures, the establishment of driving rules, a network of garages and gas stations, the recruitment of police officers, and more. The associated milieu that allows money to be liquid (and fungible), to circulate freely, to accomplish its instrumental functions at all times in all places, is no less complex in terms of equipment than the one that allows the Golf to move. Appropriate legislation and regulation, banking networks, emitting institutions, central banks, administrative authorities, civil and criminal legal codes, juridical institutions, the Serious Fraud Office (UK), or the Federal Trade Commission (USA) — these are some of the elements that must be assembled to provide money with the environment it needs in order to function. Therefore, not one of the four functions than can be eventually fulfilled by money can be described as an intrinsic property. This is the reason why the Aristotelian conception does not hold water: it forgets the necessity of an appropriate associated milieu. To act as money, an entity should be a finely tuned assemblage of material and institutional components. Money is neither a mere institution nor a mere material. It is an entanglement of both. Money without associated milieu is no longer money.
为使这种奇特的生成得以发生，货币必须具备一种新品质，人们颇具暗示性地称之为“流动性”（liquidity）。

流动性（可大可小：存在“流动性程度”）衡量的是它维持并有较大机会成功履行其功能的能力（大小）。如果货币（商品地位的候选者）无法在日后某个时候、在另一个地方被用作支付手段，如果它的价值得不到保持，我怀疑我的借款人会愿意掏出钱（他将付给我的利息）来取得使用它的权利。货币通过其功能，使某些行动（买、卖、囤积等等）得以完成。要转化为商品，必要且充分的条件是：采取这些行动的能力在时间中和空间中得到了保证。因此，它与我们先前考察的大众高尔夫（Volkswagen Golf）并无根本不同。和汽车一样，货币需要一个使它的用途成为可能的关联环境。要行驶，高尔夫除其他条件外，还需要道路基础设施、驾驶规则的制定、修车厂与加油站网络、警察的招募，等等。使货币具有流动性（以及可替代性）、自由流通、随时随地履行其工具功能的关联环境，在装备的复杂程度上丝毫不亚于使高尔夫得以行驶的关联环境。适当的立法与监管、银行网络、发行机构、中央银行、行政当局、民事与刑事法典、司法机构、英国严重欺诈办公室（Serious Fraud Office）、美国联邦贸易委员会（Federal Trade Commission）——这些只是必须装配起来、以便为货币提供其运作所需环境的部分要素。因此，货币最终能够履行的四项功能中，没有一项可以被描述为内在属性。这就是亚里士多德式观念站不住脚的原因：它忘记了适当关联环境的必要性。要作为货币发挥作用，一个实体应当是物质成分与制度成分精细调校的装配。货币既不只是制度，也不只是物质。它是二者的缠结。没有关联环境的货币不再是货币。

Then we can push further the comparison between Golf and money. Imagine a country with little road infrastructure, made up of vast desert stretches crossed by impetuous and unpredictable rivers and without garages or mechanics with the know-how to provide rapid and efficient repairs to a car after an accident. We can be confident that in such an environment, the latest trendy Golf, stuffed with electronics, devilishly urban with its integrated GPS, low-profile tires, reduced ground clearance, backup radars useful for parking in the small, crowded streets of the capital city, would seem quite simply poorly adapted. Anyone who dreams of adventure, daring crossings of overflowing wadis and nights sleeping on a vehicle roof to guard against great cats, will not give a Golf even a second glance. He will skip the Volkswagen hatchback and make a beeline for the Land Rovers, for four-wheel drives able to withstand the hardest trials and most extreme conditions.

然后我们可以进一步推进高尔夫与货币之间的比较。想象一个道路基础设施稀少的国家，由广袤的沙漠地带构成，其间有湍急难测的河流穿过，也没有修车厂或具备技术能力的机械师，能在事故后为汽车提供快速有效的修理。我们可以确信，在这样的环境里，最新款、塞满电子设备、十足都市化的高尔夫——配有集成 GPS、低扁平比轮胎、降低的离地间隙、便于在首都狭窄拥挤街道上停车的倒车雷达——会显得简直不合时宜。任何梦想冒险、敢于穿越泛滥干谷（wadi）、在车顶过夜以防大型猫科动物的人，都不会看高尔夫一眼。他会越过大众的掀背车，直奔路虎（Land Rover），直奔那些能经受最艰难考验与最极端条件的四轮驱动车。

The same goes for money. Would it not make sense to draw a distinction between four-wheel drive or all-terrain currencies, apt at fulfilling some of what has been progressively counted as their basic functions in under-equipped and threatening environments, and high-tech currencies that offer a diversified range of features and circulate smoothly in milieus that are heavily endowed with institutions and infrastructures of all sorts, such that they can fully exploit their qualities? It makes sense, then, to consider that there are, on the one hand, precious metals, not yet turned into coins, fulfilling their role as means of payment, reserves of worth, and so on more or less well (to be fair: pretty well) in a rather hostile environment; and, on the other hand, there are electronically loaded currencies circulating at light speed, transforming back and forth between credits and assets, that owe it to their “hypercivilized” associated milieu that they preserve all the instrumental functions.

货币也是如此。把“四轮驱动”或全地形货币——它们在装备不足、充满威胁的环境中，善于履行人们逐渐视为其基本功能的部分功能——与高科技货币区分开来，难道没有意义吗？后者提供多样化的功能，在充斥着各类制度与基础设施的环境中顺畅流通，因而能够充分发挥其品质。因此，合理的看法是：一方面，有尚未铸成硬币的贵金属，它们在相当敌意的环境中或多或少地（公平地说：相当好地）履行支付手段、价值贮藏等功能；另一方面，有以光速流通、在信用与资产之间来回转化的电子货币，它们之所以能保持全部工具功能，要归功于其“高度文明化”的关联环境。

It would doubtless be easy to situate along this continuum running from all-terrain currencies to the high-tech ones a series of monies that establish variable compromises between aptitude for liquidity, on one side, and effi -ciency in their instrumental functions, on the other. The outcome would depend on how their material characteristics and their associated milieus are arranged, or using the terms I proposed above, depending on the balance they achieve between autonomy and independence. Banknotes are no doubt situated halfway between the extreme poles. They shift more easily and faster between one function and another than do masses of precious metal, thus demonstrating a greater aptitude for liquidity. In return, they require a better-equipped and richer-associated milieu: circulating faster than metals, they wear out faster (issuing institutions establish programs to renew them periodically); they travel less far because the creation of unified monetary zones (with currencies that serve as accounting units, such as the European Currency Unit, which then have to be transformed into legal tender such as the euro) is an expensive, endless project. Symmetrically, a banknote is less liquid, but less demanding in terms of associated milieu, than electronic money. The reader can pursue the analysis to decide how to assign positions to Old Master paintings or collector stamps. The conclusion would no doubt be, as it is for the authors of economics textbooks who love these sorts of examples: as a means of payment, a Rembrandt painting has serious disadvantages. For instance, even if I manage to transport it, I am not sure that my neighborhood car dealer will be open to accepting it without further discussion as payment for the four-wheel drive I wish to acquire. He would, however, recognize that as a store of value, the Rembrandt does a pretty good job and would furthermore observe that to fulfill both functions in the long term requires a highly specialized associated milieu whose constitution is perforce slow and costly (existence of a milieu of experts and amateurs, organization of auctions, and so on).

In other words, a wide range of hybrid currencies exist, torn between their instrumental functions and their status as commodities, just as in the car market, one finds an array of real fake urban four-wheel-drive vehicles not really up to the task of crossing riverbeds, but nonetheless capable of negotiating the rocky back roads in Corsica, of parking smoothly on Paris sidewalks, and of giving their drivers a panoramic view that serves to reassure.

沿着这条从全地形货币到高科技货币的连续统，无疑可以容易地安置一系列货币，它们在流动性与工具功能效率之间达成不同程度的妥协。结果取决于其物质特征与关联环境如何安排，或者用我上文提出的术语，取决于它们在自主与独立之间达成的平衡。纸币无疑位于两个极端之间。它们比大块贵金属更容易、更快速地在一种功能与另一种功能之间转换，从而显示出更强的流动性。作为回报，它们要求装备更好、更丰富的关联环境：它们比金属流通得更快，也磨损得更快（发行机构制定定期更换计划）；它们能走的路程更短，因为建立统一货币区（其货币充当记账单位，例如欧洲货币单位〔European Currency Unit〕，随后又须转化为欧元这样的法定货币）是一项昂贵而无止境的事业。对称地，纸币比电子货币流动性更低，但对关联环境的要求也更低。读者可以继续这一分析，来决定如何为古典大师绘画（Old Master paintings）或收藏邮票定位。结论无疑会像那些喜爱此类例子的经济学教科书作者所说的那样：作为支付手段，伦勃朗（Rembrandt）的画作有严重缺陷。例如，即便我设法把它运过去，我也不确定街区的汽车经销商会愿意不加讨论地接受它，作为我想买的那辆四轮驱动车的付款。然而他会承认，作为价值贮藏，伦勃朗做得相当不错；他还会指出，要在长期中同时履行两种功能，需要一个高度专业化的关联环境，而其建立必然缓慢而昂贵（存在专家与业余爱好者的圈子、拍卖的组织，等等）。
换言之，存在着广泛的混合货币，它们被撕裂于工具功能与商品地位之间；正如在汽车市场上，人们能找到一批真假参半的城市四轮驱动车，它们其实并不真的胜任穿越河床，却仍能在科西嘉（Corsica）崎岖的后路上行驶，在巴黎人行道上平稳停车，并给驾驶者一种令人安心的全景视野。

The experts in monetary techniques have noted the existence of this tension and the extreme forms of currency to which it leads. As opposed to the aforementioned commodity currencies (such as precious metals), they speak of
fiat money

to designate the currencies with high liquidity and fungibility (banknotes, lines of credit, and so on): in order to function as an instrument of money, these monies indeed require institutions conceived so as to create the confidence that guarantees their continuity. It is possible to insist on the issue of confidence (the French expression is in fact
monnaie fiduciaire

, fiduciary currency),but we should then also talk about confidence in the case of the latest Golf: the buyer knows, without having to do complicated research, that he will be able to use it in the city and on the highway. That confidence originates in the very existence of an associated milieu adapted to the good’s characteristics, whether it is a car or a currency.
The milieu should therefore be put under the spotlight. I will come back to the confidence issue in Chapter 5, devoted to
affectio mercatus
货币技术专家已经注意到这种张力的存在，以及它导致的极端货币形式。与前述商品货币（如贵金属）相对，他们用“法定货币”（
fiat money
）来指称具有高流动性与可替代性的货币（纸币、信贷额度等等）：为了作为货币工具发挥作用，这些货币确实需要一些制度，这些制度被构想出来，是为了创造保证其连续性的信任。人们可以坚持强调信任问题（法语说法实际上是
monnaie fiduciaire
，即信用货币），但若如此，我们也应当谈论最新款高尔夫的信任问题：买主无需做复杂研究就知道，他能在城市和高速公路上使用它。这种信任源自一个与物品特性相适应的关联环境的实际存在，无论该物品是汽车还是货币。
因此，应当把关联环境置于聚光灯下。我将在第5章讨论
affectio mercatus
（市场情动）时回到信任问题。

The reader will have understood that liquidity, its faculty of circulating without losing at least some its different functionalities, is not without connection with money’s material characteristics, just as the car is technically different, depending on whether it aspires to be recognized as an off-road vehicle or as a simple city car.
读者想必已经理解，流动性——即货币在流通中至少仍能保有若干不同功能的能力——并非与货币的物质特征无关，正如汽车在技术上有所不同，取决于它想被承认为越野车还是普通城市车。

Here is my hypothesis: the more that the material qualities of a currency render it (potentially) adept at accomplishing its four functions almost simultaneously and with the same efficiency, the more it is likely to become a commodity. However, it will also require a rich, complex, and diversified associated milieu for these capacities to be effectively exercised. Conversely, the more laborious that fulfilling of its functions is, the more it struggles to move from one function to another, the less it is liquid and the less its function as a currency instrument calls for a heavily equipped associated milieu, but the more it is difficult to transform into a commodity. On the one hand, light electronic currency, liquid and demanding, on the other, the heavy masses of precious metals, viscous and accommodating.

以下是我的假设：一种货币的物质品质越是使它（潜在地）善于以同等效率几乎同时完成四项功能，它就越可能成为商品。然而，它也将需要一个丰富、复杂而多样的关联环境，这些能力才能被有效行使。反之，履行其功能越是费力，它越难从一种功能转向另一种功能，流动性越低，其作为货币工具的功能对装备精良的关联环境的要求也越低，但它越难转化为商品。一方面，是轻盈的电子货币，流动而苛求；另一方面，是沉重的贵金属，黏滞而随和。

To make the connection with the repertoire of market passiva(c)tion, one further observation is necessary. The set of specifications for market passiva(c)tion indeed requires that transferable property rights be attributed. There again, even a rapid inspection shows that the qualities of the currency as it emerges from its interactions with its associated milieu count. Question: Who is the owner of the piece of precious metal that is offered to me in return for the good I wish to sell? The answer is problematic, given how much the trajectory and the biography of this piece of metal, including probable thefts and misappropriations, are likely to have been long and disrupted. It is hard to trace it from its extraction to this day when I am enjoined to accept it as a means of payment. Question: Who really owns the banknote that, given my reticence, my client decides to pull out of his briefcase? The answer is simpler and quicker: the “bearer” of the bill is reputed to be its owner, provided that an adequate associated milieu does exist. Attribution and commutation are even easier in the case of electronic money and particularly in the use of mobile phones, suitably reconfigured, as means of payment and transfers.

Holders of bank accounts can easily assert their property rights on the wealth they have amassed because their accounts are held by hardware and legal assemblages (lines of code, networks of inscriptions, computers, transmission infrastructures . . . that require more sophisticated competencies and tools to be cracked than any safe deposit box). If, however, perchance one chose Old Master paintings as currency, one would have to be in a position to gather rapidly and lug around a bunch of documents that ensured that it was indeed a Rembrandt and that guaranteed property rights. High liquidity, which, as we have seen, encourages commodification, also facilitates attribution and transfer of property rights.

要与市场被动化的清单建立联系，还需作进一步观察。市场被动化的一套规格确实要求归属可转让的财产权。在这里，快速检视同样表明，货币在与关联环境互动中产生的品质至关重要。问题：那块被提供给我、以换取我想出售之物品的贵金属，归谁所有？答案很成问题，因为这块金属的轨迹与传记——包括很可能发生过的盗窃与侵占——或许漫长而颠沛。要追溯它从开采到如今我被要求接受它为支付手段的这一天，十分困难。问题：当我的客户见我犹豫，决定从公文包里掏出的那张纸币，究竟归谁所有？答案更简单、更迅速：纸币的“持票人”被推定为它的所有者，条件是存在一个适当的关联环境。在电子货币的情形中，尤其是在把经过适当重新配置的手机用作支付与转账手段时，归属与转换更加容易。
银行账户持有人可以轻易主张对其积累财富的财产权，因为他们的账户由硬件与法律装配所持有（代码行、铭写网络、计算机、传输基础设施……要破解它们，比撬开任何保险箱都需要更复杂的能力与工具）。然而，倘若有人选择古典大师绘画作为货币，他就必须能够迅速收集并随身携带一捆文件，以确认它确实是伦勃朗的作品，并担保财产权。高流动性——正如我们所见，它鼓励商品化——也便利了财产权的归属与转让。

This detour may have seemed a little long and tedious, but it was necessary to understand the inherent difficulties in transforming money into a commodity and the role that material properties play. Luckily, it leads to a simple proposition, which can be expressed as follows: the market passiva(c)tion of money requires an associated milieu that is all the more complex, heavily equipped, and costly as its properties make money fit to accomplish its different instrumental functions efficiently and effectively. The same movement that increases its performances as instrument money favors its transformation into a commodity. However, this transformation subjects its bearers to considerable risk unless the associated milieu required for it to continue to function as instrument money is conceived and set up with the greatest attention and professionalism. The history of money is at least in part the history of a long succession of necessarily imperfect solutions and arrangements imagined to handle this recurring tension.

这段绕道也许显得有点长、有点乏味，但要理解把货币转化为商品所固有的困难，以及物质属性所扮演的角色，它是必要的。幸运的是，它导向一个简单的命题，可以表述如下：货币的市场被动化需要一个关联环境，而货币的属性越是使它能高效、有效地完成其不同工具功能，这个关联环境就越是复杂、装备越是精良、成本越是高昂。同一运动既提高了它作为工具货币的性能，也促进了它向商品的转化。然而，除非为使它继续作为工具货币运作所需的关联环境被极其审慎而专业地构想和建立起来，否则这一转化就会使其持有者承受相当大的风险。货币史至少部分地是一连串必然不完美的解决方案与安排的历史，这些方案与安排被设想出来，以应对这一反复出现的张力。

Carried by technological innovations, money wants only to flow, to live its own life, to stray from the paths traced for it and the instrument roles assigned to it. Money, which is chosen and profiled to serve simultaneously as a store of value, means of payment, and accounting unit simply by virtue of its mobility, its divisibility, its immutability, the ease with which it can be accumulated, its traceability, and its liquidity, constantly suggests courses of action (those of commodities) for which it had not been necessarily programmed, but into which, with the complicity of its bearers, it shifts without further ado. Money stimulates sales by setting up the complementary roles of buyer and seller, it acquires sometimes a general value and gives legitimate access (as theft does not) to all sorts of good. Because it makes acquisition possible, money heats up minds, fans passions, greed, and usurious loans. It becomes even more active as it becomes an asset (
actif
) and provokes speculative fever.

Whereas one might want to confine it to the role of a technical instrument, it spills over into other roles. Whatever measures are taken, it always manages, somehow or other, to escape from the framework some would like to impose on it and to become the object of commercial transactions. Money, engaged in the process of commodification, flows, slips away, ebbs, insinuates itself, spreads, contracts, and dilates like quicksilver. Money is something to track down, to attempt to get hold of; one lends it, demanding that it return enlarged by its interest. It makes debts that are paid back, capital plus interest. It is invested to produce more than what was invested. It buys on credit and brings in the profits for playing a bull market. Money thus engenders money as a living being perpetuates itself endlessly, multiplying in its progeny. You thought it was here, and suddenly it is gone; now you see it, now you don’t. Money is never as inclined to stray from its state of being a well-framed instrument (its function is to count, change, pay, and store value), to edge closer to the status of goods transferable in return for compensation of the monetary sort and to tip over into the sphere of commodification at the very moment when it best fulfills its instrumental functions. The properties of money make it into a permanent provocation. Although it was profiled to serve —that is, to initiate determined and controllable actions, by virtue of the very qualities conferred on it, it suddenly transforms irresistibly into the master and intrudes into the intimacy of those who seize it. There is nothing fictitious about these successive transformations, which make money into a full-blown commodity. Money makes those who possess it and who are possessed by it act almost unwittingly. It is not surprising that it should have become a central character in dramatic literature from Aristophanes’s
Wasps
to Tom Wolfe’s
Bonfire of the Vanities
or Émile Zola’s
The Kill
. Money can, of course, bring about altruistic acts, but if Apuleius’s ass were to return, it would attest that money generates more serious crimes than acts of generosity.

在技术创新的推动下，货币只想流动，只想过自己的生活，只想偏离为它划定的路径和指派给它的工具角色。货币被选中、被塑造为同时充当价值贮藏、支付手段与记账单位，仅仅凭借其可移动性、可分割性、不可腐坏性、易于积累、可追溯性与流动性；它不断提示出一些它未必被程序设定的行动方案（商品的方案），而它在其持有者的共谋下，索性滑入其中。货币通过设置买方与卖方的互补角色来刺激销售；它有时获得一种普遍价值，并赋予人们以正当途径（不同于偷窃）接触各类物品的机会。由于它使获取成为可能，货币使头脑发热，煽动激情、贪婪与高利贷。它越成为资产（
actif
），就越活跃，并引发投机狂潮。

人们或许想把它限制在技术工具的角色中，它却溢出到其他角色。无论采取什么措施，它总能以某种方式逃离有人想强加给它的框架，成为商业交易的标的。卷入商品化过程的货币，像水银一样流动、滑走、退潮、渗入、扩散、收缩、膨胀。货币是应予追踪、试图抓住的东西；人们把它借出，要求它带着利息增长后归来。它制造被偿还的债务——本金加利息。它被投资，以产出多于所投入的东西。它赊购，并从做多市场中带来利润。于是货币生出货币，如同一个活的存在者无尽地自我延续，在其后代中增殖。你以为它在这里，它却忽然不见了；此刻见它，转眼不见。货币最完美地履行其工具功能的那一刻，也正是它最容易偏离其被良好框定的工具状态（其功能是计数、兑换、支付与贮藏价值）、走向可换取货币性补偿的可转移物品地位，并进入商品化领域的时候。货币的属性使它成为一种永恒的挑衅。尽管它被塑造为服务于人——即启动确定且可控的行动——但凭借赋予它的那些品质，它突然不可抗拒地转化为主人，并闯入抓取它的人的私密之中。这些接连不断的转化，使货币成为十足的商品，其中没有任何虚构之处。货币使那些拥有它、又被它占有的人几乎不知不觉地行动。难怪它会成为戏剧文学的中心人物，从阿里斯托芬（Aristophanes）的《马蜂》（
Wasps
）到汤姆·沃尔夫（Tom Wolfe）的《虚荣的篝火》（
Bonfire of the Vanities
），或埃米尔·左拉（Émile Zola）的《贪欲》（
The Kill
）。货币当然能引发利他行为，但倘若阿普列尤斯（Apuleius）的驴重返人间，它会证明：货币制造的严重罪行多于慷慨之举。

Over a long period and throughout many trials, it turned out that the coevolving transformations of monies and of their associated milieus, up to electronic currency, have gradually increased liquidity. This evolution, money’s process of passiva(c)tion, has been viable only because it has been narrowly framed. Unless it is held in check, excess liquidity is a permanent threat that ends up bringing general devastation as it transforms into impetuous torrents. Conversely, insufficient liquidity paralyzes investments and risk taking. How can one take advantage of what money allows and suggests one does without being totally submerged? In answer to this nagging question, through numerous vicissitudes, controversies, conflicts, and trials, devices and solutions have been imagined, tested, and imposed over time and in different places. How far should one agree to go in the process of commodification of money and its transformation into an asset (
actif

)? This (fifth) function, hitherto less visible but now central, that of financial instrument born of the successful combination of the four prior ones, must itself be properly mastered. If it is not, it devastates everything. Liquidity always raises the question of the appropriate damming measures.

在长时段中、历经许多考验，货币及其关联环境的共同演化——直至电子货币——逐渐提高了流动性。这一演化，即货币的被动化过程，之所以可行，仅仅因为它受到严密的框定。除非受到约束，过剩的流动性始终是一种威胁，当它转化为湍急的洪流时，最终会带来普遍性的破坏。反之，流动性不足则使投资与承担风险陷入瘫痪。如何才能利用货币所容许、所提示的行动，而不被彻底淹没？为回答这个纠缠不休的问题，历经无数波折、争论、冲突与考验，各种装置与解决方案在不同的时间与地点被设想、试验并强行确立。在货币商品化、及其转化为资产（
actif
）的过程中，人们应当同意走到多远？这一（第五项）功能——迄今不那么显眼、如今却居于中心，即由前四项功能成功结合而生的金融工具功能——本身必须被妥善驾驭。若不能，它就会摧毁一切。流动性总会提出适当筑坝的问题。

The most frequent strategies are to let monies proliferate while organizing their functional specialization and somehow limiting their aptitude for playing all roles at once. This strategy is all the easier to implement — because a given currency, even if it has appropriate and carefully profiled characteristics, is never perfectly versatile and can respond only very imperfectly and very partially to all the functions expected of it. There is no such thing as an allpurpose money.
最常见的策略，是让各种货币增殖，同时组织其功能专业化，并以某种方式限制它们同时扮演所有角色的能力。这一策略实施起来更容易，因为一种给定货币即便具备适当而经过精心塑造的特征，也从来不是完美通用的，只能非常不完美、非常部分地回应人们对它的全部功能期待。世上不存在全用途货币。

Any textbook on financial institutions will confirm this. At least three categories of distinct monetary masses are defined. The first, M1, whose stock evolves from day to day, corresponds to the money used in transactions: it includes available cash and instantaneously available deposits, such as checking accounts. The second, M2, includes M1 and the money that requires a managed conversion in order to be used in transactions, such as savings accounts. Finally M3, a third form of money (beyond M2), includes not only M1 and M2, but also financial instruments such as credit cards that allow for limited payments in a certain time period.
These different monetary masses and therefore types of money correspond to functional specialization.

In certain countries, these differences have been reinforced by regulation that forbids banks to engage in short-term speculation with their own funds or forces them to choose between managing assets and managing the deposits of means of payment.
任何一本关于金融机构的教科书都会证实这一点。至少定义了三种不同的货币总量。第一种是 M1，其存量逐日变化，对应于交易中使用的货币：它包括可用现金和可即时使用的存款，例如活期账户。第二种是 M2，包括 M1 以及需要经过管理性转换才能用于交易的货币，例如储蓄账户。最后是 M3，第三种货币形式（在 M2 之外），不仅包括 M1 和 M2，还包括信用卡之类允许在特定时段内进行有限支付的金融工具。
这些不同的货币总量、因而不同的货币类型，对应于功能专业化。
在某些国家，这些差异因监管而得到强化：监管禁止银行用自有资金从事短期投机，或迫使它们在管理资产与管理支付手段存款之间作出选择。

A simple way of controlling the tendency money has of slipping without warning from its role as an instrument to that of a commodity is to clamp down in a strict and permanent way on its instrumental qualities or to even go so far as to forbid some of them. For example, its aptitude to transform into a commodity can be compromised by making it less easily divisible, by forbidding it to be a universal means of payment, or by hampering its convertibility. Polanyi observed that both in traditional societies and in so-called modern societies, several material forms of money coexist, each being assigned exclusively to certain types of goods.

Archaeologists report that the Vikings who settled in southeastern England in the ninth century organized the coexistence of their own money, made of silver masses of differing weights, which was used in the countryside, and the native money, reserved for urban transactions, which was made of silver coins. In France, the
pièces jaunes

, small-denomination coins collected to finance a foundation serving the public good, or the silver coins put aside for grandchildren, attest to such ongoing practices. Similarly, within the private space of households, money that comes from the salaries of family members may be earmarked for certain specific uses: one portion of a spouse’s paycheck may be allocated to the other as pocket money; the internship stipends paid to an adolescent whose parents cover his tuition or the unexpected thirteenth month earned by the young person who still lives with their parents may be reserved for household expenses.

Natasha Schüll tells the story of a gambler who, having received a large sum of money at the death of her young son — a death for which she felt partially responsible because her addiction prevented her from taking proper care of him — explained that she had no other option but to deplete it in casinos because she would not have wanted to take advantage of it herself.

Bruce Carruthers and Arthur Stinchcombe observe that just like households, organizations distribute their funds into categories, certain sums being more fungible — that is to say, usable more widely, than others. (For instance, they create strategic reserves or forbid access to them by higher rungs of the hierarchy.)

The money the Japanese state collects from betting on horse races goes to scientific research. Money’s use is often related to the way it was acquired: dirty money requires laundering. As Viviana Zelizer puts it, the practices that frame and limit the instrumental functions of money lead to the constitution of special monies characterized by narrowly specialized uses.

The resulting restrictions, which can institute serious constraints, as in the case of so-called local currencies, have the effect of making the transformation of money into a commodity less likely. More generally, money, whether in the form of coins or bills, savings accounts or bank checks, credit cards or bills of exchange, can be assigned to different types of transactions. For example, by using its material properties, “plastic” money — plastic, indeed, but stuffed with electronics that give it the capacity to memorize, retrace, and add up transactions — can be reprogrammed, for example as credit cards or debit cards, depending on the various associated milieus in which it is made active. Privilege may be given to the credit function (store of value) or almost exclusively to the debit function (means of payment). These different orientations were all the easier to implement because the functions attributed to this hybrid, combining polymers and silicon, depend only on specific architectures of data flows that are designed before the cards can carry credit in place of debit.
一种控制货币从工具角色不知不觉滑向商品角色之倾向的简单方法，是严格而持久地钳制其工具品质，甚至禁止其中某些品质。例如，可以通过使货币不易分割、禁止它成为普遍支付手段、或阻碍其可兑换性，来削弱其转化为商品的能力。波兰尼观察到，无论在传统社会还是在所谓现代社会，都并存着若干物质形式的货币，每一种都被专门指派给某些类型的物品。
考古学家报告说，9世纪定居于英格兰东南部的维京人，组织了其自身货币与本地货币的并存：前者由重量不等的银块制成，用于乡村；后者专供城市交易，由银币制成。在法国，“黄硬币”（
pièces jaunes
）——为资助一个服务公益的基金会而收集的小面额硬币——或为孙辈存下的银币，都证明了这类持续存在的实践。同样，在家庭的私人空间里，来自家庭成员薪水的钱可能被指定用于某些特定用途：配偶工资的一部分可能作为零花钱分配给另一方；支付给一个由父母承担学费的青少年的实习津贴，或仍与父母同住的年轻人意外获得的第十三个月工资，可能被留作家庭开支。
娜塔莎·舒尔（Natasha Schüll）讲述了一个赌徒的故事：她在幼子去世后得到一大笔钱——她觉得自己对这场死亡负有部分责任，因为她的成瘾使她无法妥善照料孩子——她解释说，自己别无选择，只能在赌场里把这笔钱耗光，因为她不愿自己从中获益。
布鲁斯·卡拉瑟斯（Bruce Carruthers）与阿瑟·斯廷奇科姆（Arthur Stinchcombe）观察到，组织与家庭一样，把资金分配到不同类别中，某些款项比其他款项更可替代——也就是说，可以更广泛地使用。（例如，它们设立战略储备，或禁止层级中较高者动用这些储备。）
日本政府从赛马投注中收取的钱，用于科学研究。货币的用途常与其获取方式相关：脏钱需要洗白。正如维维安娜·泽利泽（Viviana Zelizer）所言，框定并限制货币工具功能的实践，导致以用途高度专门化为特征的“特殊货币”的构成。

由此产生的限制——在所谓地方货币的情形中，这些限制可能构成严重约束——具有降低货币转化为商品之可能性的效果。更一般地说，货币无论以硬币或纸币、储蓄账户或银行支票、信用卡或汇票的形式出现，都可以被指派给不同类型的交易。例如，利用其物质属性，“塑料”货币——确实是塑料，但塞满电子元件，使之能够记忆、回溯和累加交易——可以被重新编程，例如作为信用卡或借记卡，取决于它被激活于其中的各种关联环境。可以优先赋予信用功能（价值贮藏），或几乎专一地赋予借记功能（支付手段）。这些不同取向之所以都容易实施，是因为赋予这种聚合物与硅之混合物的功能，只取决于在卡片能够以信用取代借记之前所设计的特定数据流架构。
Local or private currencies such as LETS,

controlled by communities of their users, are generally characterized by strict regulation and even the complete outlawing of certain of their functions: bills are useable only as a means of payment within a strictly delimited collective; they cannot give rise to loans; there are rules about their convertibility to other currencies; unusable after a certain date, they cannot be used as a store of value. All sorts of configurations can be imagined.
The credit cards put into circulation by big distribution companies are private monies for the impecunious whose functions (payment, credit, obtaining cash) are strictly regulated.

The findings are unanimous. All-terrain currencies able to fulfill the four functions that have ended up being assigned to them in all places and at all times — all-purpose money, in other words — simply cannot exist. In each currency, there is a sleeping Rembrandt just waiting to be roused from its slumber!
由使用者共同体控制的本地货币或私人货币，如 LETS（本地交换交易系统），
通常以严格规制、甚至完全取缔其某些功能为特征：纸币只能在严格限定的集体内部作为支付手段使用；它们不能引发借贷；关于它们与其他货币的兑换有规则；在某些日期之后不可使用，因而不能充当价值贮藏。各种配置都可以想象。
大型分销公司发行的信用卡，是面向囊中羞涩者的私人货币，其功能（支付、信贷、取得现金）受到严格规制。
研究结论是一致的。能够在任何地点、任何时间履行最终指派给它们的四项功能的全地形货币——换言之，全用途货币——根本不可能存在。在每一种货币中，都睡着一个伦勃朗，只待从沉睡中被唤醒！

Such measures of specialization, demarcation, territorialization, and interdiction localize money, fragment its uses, and decouple its functions. They thereby generate another opposition, which adds to the impression of splintering: that between private and public monies. This opposition has considerable effects. The former tend to limit or control money’s propensity to transform into a commodity and activate financial strategies. The latter, on the contrary, facilitate this transformation by providing a vast circulation space and guaranteeing, through rules aimed at reducing the uncertainties associated with its use and by multiplying specialized monies and appropriated rules of conversion between them, that the four functions be correctly fulfilled and contribute to increased and supposedly well-framed liquidity.

这类专业化、划界、领域化与禁止的措施，使货币地方化，分割其用途，并使其功能彼此脱钩。它们由此产生另一种对立，加深了支离破碎的印象：私人货币与公共货币之间的对立。这一对立具有相当大的效应。前者倾向于限制或控制货币转化为商品、激活金融策略的倾向。后者相反，通过提供一个广阔的流通空间，并通过旨在减少与其使用相关的不确定性的规则、以及通过使专门化货币和它们之间适当的兑换规则成倍增加，来保证四项功能得到正确履行，并有助于提高那种据称得到良好框定的流动性。

The different damming actions I have sketched explain why currencies are always multiple, each being called on to fulfill certain functions, rather than others. This observation holds not only for traditional societies, but equally and especially for those described as advanced. When a certain type of currency, for instance, that attached to the function of payment, is lacking, specialized monies very quickly will appear to compensate for its weaknesses, or counterfeit currency will fill the gap. The multiplication of monies and their regulation is the result of initiatives that in large measure escape government control, despite their massive involvement in monetary policy. Everywhere one can observe monies that are multiple, fragmented, specialized, hierarchized, and supported by user communities that are separate from one another. The recent development of so-called cryptocurrencies shows how certain technologies such as blockchains have forced central banks to react so as not to imperil their monetary sovereignty.
Those private monies raise, like the libra, the crucial question of their conversion, often surrounded with phenomena that bring about exclusion.

With my revenues as a (retired) academic, I regularly use M1, a little M2, and extremely rarely M3, to which I have only indirect and costly access. Local and specialized money confines its users within borders that are difficult to transgress. The Uzbek farmer who sells his cotton to state companies will have a hard time converting the money from his sales into dollars.

我所勾勒的不同筑坝行动，解释了为什么货币总是多样的，每一种都被要求履行某些功能而非另一些功能。这一观察不仅适用于传统社会，同样、尤其适用于那些被称为发达的社会。当某一类货币——例如与支付功能相连的货币——缺失时，专门化货币很快就会冒出来弥补其弱点，或者伪币会填补空缺。货币的增殖及其规制，是很大程度上逃逸于政府控制之外的举措的结果，尽管政府在货币政策中深度介入。到处都可以观察到多样、碎片化、专门化、等级化的货币，它们由彼此分离的使用者共同体支撑。所谓加密货币的晚近发展表明，区块链等技术如何迫使中央银行作出反应，以免危及其货币主权。
这些私人货币，如天秤币（libra），提出了其兑换这一关键问题，而兑换往往伴随着导致排斥的现象。
以我作为（退休）学者的收入，我经常使用 M1，少量使用 M2，极少使用 M3——我只能间接且昂贵地接触 M3。地方货币与专门化货币把使用者禁闭在难以逾越的边界之内。把棉花卖给国有公司的乌兹别克农民，将很难把销售所得货币兑换成美元。

The proliferation of devices aimed at containing money’s propensity to provoke financial activities leads to remarkable results that calm the concerns it raises. The problem, as some see it, is that containment durably weakens the money’s efficacy. Speculation can be avoided by playing on the properties of a currency, but how far should one go in this exercise of self-defense? A currency that is allowed at least to a certain extent to transform into an asset (
actif

) — that is, to be active as a commodity, opens the way to courses of action, initiatives, and (ad)ventures that would otherwise be impossible. How is the right equilibrium to be found? How can money be authorized to be active, but not too active? This is not a new question. It has been the subject of erudite and moral reflection for centuries. Aristotle, the Church Fathers, and the successive commentators of the Koran, among others, warned against the damaging effects of this apparently crazy practice of making money into a sort of living being able to engender itself and multiply itself via interest rates; they tried to propose acceptable accommodations.
旨在遏制货币引发金融活动之倾向的装置大量增殖，带来了平息其引发的忧虑的显著结果。问题在于，在某些人看来，遏制会持久地削弱货币的效力。可以通过操纵一种货币的属性来避免投机，但这种自卫演习应当走到多远？一种至少在一定程度上被允许转化为资产（
actif
）——即作为商品而活跃——的货币，打开了通往否则不可能的行动方案、举措与冒险的道路。如何找到正确的平衡？如何能授权货币活跃，但又不过分活跃？这不是新问题。几个世纪以来，它一直是博学与道德反思的主题。亚里士多德、教父们以及《古兰经》的历代注释者等，都警告过这种看似疯狂的做法的破坏性后果——使货币成为某种能够通过利率自我生成、自我增殖的活物；他们试图提出可接受的调适方案。

We are still facing the dilemma. Granted, money has such mobilizing force that it can produce nefarious and dangerous effects. However, it is also such a force in mobilizing and liberating energies that it would be a shame to neutralize its dynamism out of prudence or fear of risk. Like a wild animal whose outbursts or rampages are feared, but whose power one tries to use by taming it, money must be domesticated. However, that must be done in a subtle and appropriate way: neither too much nor too little. In short, what is at stake is preserving the faculty money has to make act beyond its strictly determined and now well-entrenched four technical functions without leaving the leeway for it to provoke (too much) disorder and chaos. Since there is no a priori recipe, this meticulous calibration between liquidity and viscosity has taken place through a long series of trial-and-error experiments; it has given rise to crises, controversies, and violent clashes, including those still happening before our very eyes.

我们仍然面对这一两难。诚然，货币具有如此强大的动员力量，以致能产生恶劣而危险的效果。然而，它在动员与解放能量方面也是一种如此强大的力量，以致出于审慎或对风险的恐惧而中和其活力，将是可惜的。就像一头野兽，人们惧怕它的暴怒或横冲直撞，却试图通过驯服来利用它的力量，货币必须被驯化。然而，这必须以一种微妙而恰当的方式进行：既不太多，也不太少。简言之，关键在于保存货币在严格确定的、如今已牢固确立的四项技术功能之外促使他者行动的能力，同时又不留下让它引发（过多）混乱与无序的余地。由于不存在先验的配方，这种在流动性与黏滞性之间的精细校准，是通过一长串试错实验完成的；它引发了危机、争论与暴力冲突，包括仍在我们眼前发生的那些。

Taming the beast — or, to put it in more graceful terms, controlling liquidity — takes time. It is ongoing, and there is no end in sight. It requires a series of technical and regulatory inventions that, through successive steps, liberate its mobilizing forces, its almost infinite capacity to incite and make act, while trying to contain them within acceptable limits in order to avoid excessively violent shocks and to maintain the possibility of its exercising its instrumental functions. Two episodes played a crucial role in this long-running story of the never-ending market passiva(c)tion of money. The first corresponds to the theological battles over interest payments: thanks to a great deal of rhetorical skill and the development of ingenious regulatory devices, these were eventually recognized, at least in certain social circles, as legitimate after having long been considered dangerous and potentially immoral.

Money now works for us, or rather for some of us. The second battle, still raging, is the one over what are now called financial instruments. Whereas the story about interest rates and their vicissitudes is widely known and documented, the one about these products of a very particular kind is still to be written. Given their contemporary importance, it is not superfluous to devote a few lines to them, because they give a compelling illustration of the logic and difficulties of the market passiva(c)tion of money. Furthermore they show the relevance of the notions I have proposed to giving an account of this process, which is central to the endless commodification of money.

驯服这头野兽——或者用更优雅的说法，控制流动性——需要时间。它正在进行，且看不到尽头。它要求一系列技术与监管发明，这些发明通过接连的步骤，释放其动员力量、其几乎无限的激发与促人行动的能力，同时试图把它们控制在可接受的限度内，以避免过于剧烈的冲击，并维持其履行工具功能的可能。在货币永无止境的市场被动化这一漫长故事中，有两个插曲起了关键作用。第一个对应于围绕利息支付的神学论战：凭借大量修辞技巧和巧妙监管装置的开发，利息最终至少在某些社会圈子里被承认为正当，而此前长期被视为危险且可能不道德的。
如今货币为我们工作，或者更确切地说，为我们中的某些人工作。第二场战斗仍在激烈进行，围绕如今所谓的金融工具展开。关于利率及其波折的故事广为人知、文献丰富，而关于这类非常特殊的产品之故事，尚待书写。鉴于它们在当代的重要性，用几行文字讨论它们并非多余，因为它们令人信服地例示了货币市场被动化的逻辑与困难。此外，它们也表明我提出的那些概念对于说明这一过程具有相关性，而这一过程对货币无尽的商品化至关重要。

Even though what are now called financial products or instruments seem to have a distant origin, it is only recently that they have been used systematically and that markets have been organized for them.

Take the case of stocks: it took a few centuries for them to behave like recognized entities that have stable and legitimate qualities and codified behavior and that can easily be detached and reattached. For instance, in France, many years went by before a space appeared for them to change hands legitimately and before the agents engaged in these transactions were authorized to leave the cafés in rue Quincampoix in Paris, to which they had been relegated and instead be admitted into what were considered honorable places. Stocks contaminated those through whose hands they passed. A genuine social prophylactic had to be set up in order to make them into commodities like any other. That required, for example, that lists of exchangeable stocks be established and imposed and that the identities of those people who could have access to the transaction be defined precisely. Alex Preda, in his history of financial markets, gives a minute description of the constitution of a world that progressively obtains the market passiva(c)tion of this strange good, this unpredictable vector for disorder and suspect passions — namely, a stock that is bought and sold and that can be promoted and accumulated. Before the passiva(c)tion was accomplished (it actually happened only at the beginning of the twentieth century, when, in 1905, accounting became compulsory for brokers on the New York Stock Exchange), and despite the huge efforts by professionals who follow stock prices, analyze the reasons for pricings, and offer tools to determine value and explain their evolution, the limit between the stock market and the casino is tenuous. Taming stocks (“
action

,” as the French language judiciously chose to name this product, underlining the need for serious regulation to prevent it acting in random directions) turned out to be difficult; it required a great deal of effort, ingeniousness, and material and institutional investments to manage things such that it neither returns to a wild state nor veers out of control.
尽管如今所谓的金融产品或金融工具似乎起源久远，但它们被系统地使用、并为之组织市场，只是晚近的事。

以股票为例：经过几个世纪，它们才表现得像被承认的实体，具有稳定而正当的品质、成文的行为规范，能够容易地脱离与再附着。例如在法国，经过许多年，才出现一个让它们合法易手的空间，从事这些交易的行动者才被授权离开巴黎坎康普瓦街（rue Quincampoix）的咖啡馆——他们曾被贬斥到那里——并被接纳进被认为是体面的场所。股票会污染经手它的人。必须建立一套真正的社会预防措施，才能使它们成为像任何其他商品一样的商品。这要求例如制定并强制实施可交易股票的名单，并精确界定哪些人有资格参与交易。亚历克斯·普雷达（Alex Preda）在其金融市场史中，细致描绘了一个世界的构成：这个世界逐渐实现了对这种奇怪物品的市场被动化——这种物品是不可预测的无序与可疑激情的载体，即一种被买卖、可以被推介和积累的股票。在被动化完成之前（它实际上直到20世纪初才完成，1905年纽约证券交易所〔New York Stock Exchange〕的经纪人被强制要求记账），尽管专业人士付出了巨大努力——他们跟踪股价、分析定价理由、提供确定价值与解释价格演化的工具——股票市场与赌场之间的界限仍然十分模糊。驯服股票（法语明智地选择“
action
”来命名这种产品，强调需要严格监管以防它朝随机方向行动）被证明是困难的；它需要大量努力、巧思以及物质与制度投资，才能把事情料理到既不会退回野蛮状态、也不会失控的地步。

Derivatives, the regulation of which is far from complete and which have developed spectacularly in the last decades, turn out to be even more difficult to tame. To stigmatize their constant overflowings and their excessive capacity for provoking courses of action that run out of control, these are sometimes referred to as toxic products or junk bonds. Their commodification is hardly a walk in the park. To illustrate some of the difficulties encountered and the devices imagined in response, I will say a few words about the beginnings of the modern history of derivatives (forward contracts) and a few of the trials and tribulations through which they had to pass before invading and colonizing financial markets.
衍生品——其监管远未完成，并在过去几十年间迅猛发展——被证明更难驯服。为了谴责其不断的溢出、以及其引发失控行动方案的过度能力，它们有时被称为有毒产品或垃圾债券。它们的商品化绝非轻而易举。为说明所遇到的一些困难以及作为回应而设想的装置，我将谈几句衍生品（远期合约〔forward contracts〕）现代史的开端，以及它们在侵入并殖民金融市场之前不得不经历的一些考验与磨难。

A forward contract allows a seller to establish the sales price of a good before the transaction actually takes place. The seller can thus protect himself against a sudden large drop in prices. The trade-off is that if prices go up, in other words, if at the moment of the transaction they are higher than the price that had been established ahead of time, the seller is deprived of the benefit of the rise. This very simple tool allows for an adjustment between buyer and seller. It is particularly useful when the prices for the goods that are the object of the transaction (the underlying goods) are irregular and unpredictable. Such volatility can have multiple causes — for instance, weather, in the case of cereals such as wheat or corn, or the fluctuations in supply and demand, as in the case of certain metals, or raw materials, or financial products such as . . . foreign currencies and interest rates. The large-scale development of forward contracts began in the middle of the nineteenth century in the United States and concerned mostly agricultural products. It gradually extended to goods such as gold and silver, sugar or petroleum. It was only in the 1970s that forward contracts became common practice in financial markets.

远期合约使卖方能够在交易实际发生之前确定一件物品的售价。卖方由此可以防范价格突然大幅下跌。代价是，如果价格上涨，也就是说，如果在交易时刻价格高于事先确定的价格，卖方就失去了上涨带来的好处。这个非常简单的工具使买方与卖方之间得以调整。当作为交易标的的物品（标的物品）价格不规则、不可预测时，它尤其有用。这种波动性可能有多种原因——例如，就小麦或玉米等谷物而言是天气；就某些金属、原材料或……外币与利率等金融产品而言，是供求的波动。远期合约的大规模发展始于19世纪中叶的美国，主要涉及农产品。它逐渐扩展到黄金、白银、糖或石油等物品。直到20世纪70年代，远期合约才成为金融市场的常规实践。

The way this tool spread resembles all stories of innovation. It revolves around a number of actors and institutions defending opposite and often incompatible interests. It is made of negotiations and compromises that lead to the gradual transformation of the tool and its requalification.

Yuval Millo has traced the main moments of this evolution — that is, of the gradual passiva(c)-tion of an entity, the forward contract, whose disentanglement and reentanglement were made easier without that leading to its becoming out of control or becoming the source of unmanageable overflowings and disorders.
这一工具的传播方式，与所有创新故事相似。它围绕若干行动者与制度展开，他们捍卫着彼此相反、往往不相容的利益。它由谈判与妥协构成，这些谈判与妥协导致工具的逐渐转化及其品质的重新界定。
尤瓦尔·米洛（Yuval Millo）追溯了这一演化的主要时刻——也就是一个实体即远期合约逐渐被动化的过程，其解缠与再纠缠变得更容易，却又不致使其失控，或成为难以驾驭的溢出与无序之源。
The first step of this requalification process involved dissociating the contract from the obligation to deliver the underlying asset.

Indeed, at the very beginning, on the Chicago Stock Exchange, when a farmer sold his wheat on the futures market, he had to deliver it to his buyer at the moment and price established by the contract. By making the price of the futures contract and what underlies it converge, this clause avoided speculation and prevented the signing of futures contracts being equivalent to a simple game of chance. However, it also brought heavy constraints on the resale of the contract to a third party before its execution, since to be able to fulfill this obligation, the operators had to buy back or sell back the contracts they had sold or bought.
这一重新界定品质过程的第一步，是把合约与交付标的资产的义务分离开来。
确实，最初在芝加哥交易所（Chicago Stock Exchange），当农民在期货市场上卖出小麦时，他必须在合约规定的时间、按规定的价格把小麦交付给买方。通过使期货合约的价格与其标的物趋同，这一条款避免了投机，防止签署期货合约等同于一场简单的碰运气游戏。然而，它也给合约在执行前转售给第三方带来了沉重约束，因为要能够履行这一义务，操作者必须回购或回售他们已经卖出或买入的合约。

These drawbacks became more problematic when people started imagining future sales of — why not? — stocks or portfolios of stocks, or even indexes. Futures contracts can act as insurance against the fluctuations to which all these goods are exposed, but their handling raises considerable problems. First, in the case of deliverable financial assets such as stocks or stock portfolios, there were witching hours in the market when transactions were realized and considerable blocks of stocks had to change hands at the same moment. The next problem with the delivery clause was insurmountable because some underlying assets, such as benchmark interest rates, have no physical existence and are therefore difficult to . . . deliver! These difficulties can be avoided by eliminating the delivery clause, but the risk of incontrollable speculative swings is then amplified, since no reality principle can be brought to bear on the agents engaged in these transactions, at least in the short term. In the end, after epic battles between the various protagonists of the financial markets, the solution adopted for mastering these new goods was the creation of institutions such as the CFTC, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission,

whose job is to strictly regulate the transactions, one of the most important innovations being the distinction drawn between real assets and synthetic assets, a distinction whose purpose is to insure against the risks produced by derivatives. A degree of regulation is achieved by technical measures such as, among others, the creation of central counterparty clearinghouses and the institution of limits on the daily fluctuations of contracts.

当人们开始设想对未来出售——为何不呢？——股票或股票组合、乃至指数时，这些缺陷变得更加棘手。期货合约可以作为针对所有这些物品所面临波动的保险，但它们的处理带来相当大的问题。首先，就股票或股票组合等可交付金融资产而言，市场会出现“巫魔时刻”（witching hours），大量股票必须在同一时刻易手。交付条款的下一个问题则无法克服，因为某些标的资产，例如基准利率，没有物理存在，因而难以……交付！这些困难可以通过取消交付条款来避免，但这样一来，无法控制的投机波动的风险就被放大了，因为至少短期内，没有任何现实原则可以作用于参与这些交易的行动者。最终，在金融市场各主角之间史诗般的争斗之后，为驾驭这些新物品而采用的解决方案，是创建商品期货交易委员会（Commodity Futures Trading Commission，CFTC）之类的机构，
其职责是严格监管交易，其中最重要的创新之一，是区分真实资产与合成资产，这一区分的目的是防范衍生品所产生的风险。一定程度的监管通过技术措施实现，其中包括建立中央对手方清算所、设置合约每日波动限幅等。

By allowing the delivery of the underlying clause to be eliminated, these devices transformed the futures contract into a financial product that could be subject to successive transactions without obligations to buy back or resell, since the different holders were freed from the requirement to deliver what underlies it. In this case, the closure of the contract gives rise to a cash settlement corresponding to the difference in price between the price at the close of the contract and the value of the asset finally observed. Thus physically disentangled and detached from the “good” and its initial holder, but also from the underlying asset to be provided to the buyer (hectoliters of grains, blocks of stock, or . . . immaterial indexes), the contract becomes an autonomous entity that can easily be sold. Its passiva(c)tion has made progress. It can pass from hand to hand, it can be transferred seamlessly from one agent to another, rendering services to its successive holders.

通过允许取消交付标的物的条款，这些装置把期货合约转化为一种可以连续交易、而无回购或回售义务的金融产品，因为不同持有人不再被要求交付其标的物。在此情形中，合约的了结产生一笔现金结算，其金额等于合约了结时的价格与最终观察到的资产价值之间的差额。于是，合约在物理上解缠、脱离于“物品”及其初始持有人，也脱离于应提供给买方的标的资产（若干百升谷物、若干股股票，或……非物质指数），成为一个可以轻易出售的自主实体。它的被动化取得了进展。它可以从一只手传到另一只手，从一个行动者无缝转移到另一个行动者，为其历任持有人提供服务。

The contract’s increased autonomy obviously raises problems. As those who insisted on the delivery of the underlying asset as a key requirement had understood, one of the problems is the risk of unbridled speculation, despite all the precautions taken. An attached contract limits this risk, but prevents it from becoming a full-blown commodity; a detached contract facilitates that mutation, but encourages the behavior that makes the stock market seem like a casino. And the more derivatives and derivatives of derivatives there are, the more the risk increases. Innovative products raise more and more complicated problems for regulation and control. (Talk of “responsible financial products” relies on a euphemism that discreetly draws attention to, without acknowledging, the fact that often they are irresponsible.) As Hsin Hin Lim, an equity derivatives and structured finance lawyer in the City of London mischievously notes, “When I look at a derivative product the probabilities are not known. At least in a casino the odds are certain.”
And in fact, the difference between the two sectors, the casinos and financial markets, is dwindling. What is amusing, and I will get back to this when I come to
affectio mercatus

, is that gambling activities followed a parallel path in their evolution. Intense investments were required for the passiva(c)tion of the strange goods they offer to progress; it worked so well that as we will see in Chapter 5, their commodification is no longer considered problematic. Attesting to the convergence of the sectors, certain hybrid products that combine gambling and finance are appearing in market activity. The development of betting exchanges (still forbidden by some countries, such as France), where one exchanges bets on ongoing competitions for monetary compensation, attests to this alignment. The more gambling activities are embedded in market activities, the harder it is to exclude financial speculation from them, even if they are difficult to regulate. The passiva(c)tion of financial products is a continuous process, and there seems to be no end in sight.

合约自主性的增强显然带来问题。正如那些坚持把交付标的资产视为关键要求的人所理解的，问题之一是无节制投机的风险，尽管采取了一切预防措施。附着的合约限制这一风险，却阻止它成为十足的商品；脱离的合约便利这一变异，却鼓励那种使股票市场看起来像赌场的行为。而且衍生品以及衍生品的衍生品越多，风险就越大。创新产品给监管与控制带来越来越复杂的问题。（谈论“负责任的金融产品”依赖一个委婉说法，它不声不响地引人注意却又不承认一个事实：这些产品往往是不负责任的。）正如伦敦金融城（City of London）的股票衍生品与结构化融资律师 Hsin Hin Lim 打趣地指出：“当我审视一个衍生品时，概率是未知的。至少在赌场里，输赢概率是确定的。”
事实上，赌场与金融市场这两个部门之间的差异正在缩小。有趣的是——我将在讨论
affectio mercatus

时回到这一点——赌博活动在其演化中走了一条平行的道路。为使它们所提供的奇怪物品的被动化取得进展，需要密集的投资；这非常成功，以致正如我们将在第5章看到的，它们的商品化不再被视为问题。某些结合赌博与金融的混合产品出现在市场活动中，证明这两个部门正在趋同。博彩交易所（betting exchanges，仍被法国等一些国家禁止）的发展——人们在其中就正在进行的比赛交换赌注，以获取金钱补偿——证明了这种趋同。赌博活动越是嵌入市场活动，就越难把金融投机从中排除，即使它们难以监管。金融产品的被动化是一个持续的过程，似乎看不到尽头。

In the history of the passiva(c)tion of financial instruments, regulation and the creation of institutions charged with implementing and enforcing it have played and continue to play a key role, as do technological and material innovations (notably in software) that allow for product design, elaboration, qualification, conservation, tracing, and transacting.

Taken together, these actions have led to a considerable increase in the liquidity of assets, but also to more complex operations, a proliferation of products, and difficulties in avoiding sudden crises or untimely overflowings. What chief architect would be conceited enough to dare claim he fully understands and masters the sources and effects of liquidity?
在金融工具被动化的历史中，监管以及负责实施和执行监管的机构的创建，已经并将继续发挥关键作用；允许产品设计、制作、品质界定、保存、追溯与交易的技术与物质创新（尤其是在软件方面）也是如此。
这些行动合在一起，导致资产流动性大幅提高，但也导致操作更复杂、产品激增，以及难以避免突发危机或不合时宜的溢出。有哪位总建筑师会自负到敢于宣称，自己完全理解并掌握了流动性的来源与效应？

Some may be surprised by my approach in these pages devoted to money and to the actions undertaken to promote its commodification and ensure control over it, more or less successfully. Why focus so much on money’s properties, on its capacity to be disentangled, made independent (but not too independent), when there is a sort of soft consensus around the idea that with the development and omnipresence of
fiat monies
, money is first and foremost a symbol, a social convention whose regulation should fall to the purest will — for instance, the political will?
一些人也许会对我这几页的做法感到惊讶：这些篇幅讨论货币，以及为促进其商品化、确保对其控制而采取的、或多或少成功的行动。为什么如此强调货币的属性、强调它被解缠、被弄得独立（但又不过分独立）的能力？毕竟，围绕以下观念存在某种软共识：随着
法定货币
的发展与无所不在，货币首先是一种符号，一种社会惯例，其规制应当归属于最纯粹的意志——例如政治意志。

In a programmatic article published in 2006, anthropologist Bill Maurer reminds us that since Plato and Aristotle, the analysis of money has constantly oscillated between two opposing interpretations.

The first one insists on its symbolic dimension, the second on its material reality. Maurer, following Keane, invites us to get rid of this binarism. In the preceding lines, I have done nothing but implement this advice. The opposition between these two sides of the coin is no longer relevant and actually disappears as soon as one takes an interest, as I have done, in the process of commodification and the transformations it implies and brings about.
在2006年发表的一篇纲领性文章中，人类学家比尔·莫勒（Bill Maurer）提醒我们，自柏拉图与亚里士多德以来，对货币的分析不断在两种相反解释之间摆动。
第一种强调其符号维度，第二种强调其物质现实。莫勒追随基恩（Keane），邀请我们摆脱这种二元论。在前面的文字中，我所做的不过是践行这一建议。硬币两面之间的对立不再有意义，而且只要人们像我这样关注商品化过程及其所意味、所带来的转化，这种对立实际上就消失了。

There is, however, nothing revolutionary about this perspective. Keynes laid the ground for it when he asserted that money does not have any intrinsic functions, but has, instead, properties that authorize certain courses of action. According to him, “money” is the name given to those entities that have an aptitude for doing or for making others do certain things, such as establishing prices or constituting reserves that can be used at a later date as means of payment. It suggests and authorizes certain courses of action, some of which have been progressively (at least partially) regulated and have become the functions expected of it and that it fulfills more or less efficiently, while others draw it in new directions by generating types of action that spill over the framework of usual functions and are harder to contain, such as those that lead it to play the role of a recognized asset. The same properties that make it an efficient servant push it toward its commodification. It nourishes speculation, speculation that is not in itself a bad thing, since it is a way to care for the future, but that can become so if it is not regulated by a painstakingly designed associated milieu. Servant, for sure, but not all that faithful!

然而，这一视角毫无革命性。凯恩斯（Keynes）为此奠定了基础，他断言货币没有任何内在功能，而是具有授权某些行动方案的属性。在他看来，“货币”是赋予那些实体的名称：它们有能力做某些事，或使别人做某些事，例如确定价格，或构成日后可用作支付手段的储备。它提示并授权某些行动方案，其中一些已被逐渐（至少部分地）规制，成为人们对它的功能期待，而它或多或少高效地履行这些功能；另一些则把它引向新方向，生成溢出通常功能框架、更难容纳的行动类型，例如那些使它扮演被承认的资产角色的行动。正是那些使它成为高效仆人的属性，把它推向商品化。它滋养投机，而投机本身并非坏事，因为它是照料未来的一种方式；但若不受一个精心设计的关联环境规制，它也可能变坏。是仆人，确实，但并不那么忠实！

Thanks to the constantly renewed work of passiva(c)tion and the regulations it institutes, the human being, land, and money have gradually been transformed into goods that can enter market transactions.

Particularly recalcitrant in the face of any attempts to make them simultaneously autonomous, active, independent, and controllable, these three groups of entities now play a strategic part in the development of market agencements, notably, those that can be characterized as capitalist. The history of their commodification, largely irreversible, shows constantly renewed trials of strength to open the way for making the most of their unique potential for action.
凭借不断更新的被动化工作及其所建立的规制，人类存在者、土地与货币逐渐被转化为能够进入市场交易的物品。
这三组实体尤其抗拒任何使它们同时变得自主、活跃、独立且可控的尝试，如今却在市场装配的发展中——尤其是那些可被称为资本主义的市场装配——扮演战略角色。它们商品化的历史在很大程度上不可逆，展现出不断更新的力量考验，以开辟道路，最大限度地利用其独特的行动潜能。

I hope the reader will have understood that I am not trying to justify these different processes. I am merely trying to identify what they have in common in order to better understand what commodification is. That said, passiva(c)-tion, like any framing, raises concerns, resistance, and alternative projects, the content of which differs according to the goods involved. It is in these confrontations that moral claims are forged and expressed, implicitly or explicitly. As an analyst, I limit myself to pointing out the existence of the latter, displaying their content, and describing how they are or are not taken into account. Certain ethical issues are at the heart of passiva(c)tion. To invoke an overused term, this is the root of what we can call market critique.

我希望读者已经理解，我并不是在为这些不同过程辩护。我只是试图辨识它们的共同之处，以便更好地理解商品化究竟是什么。话虽如此，被动化如同任何框定一样，会引发关切、抵抗与替代方案，其内容因所涉物品而异。正是在这些交锋中，道德主张被锻造出来，并以隐含或明确的方式得到表达。作为分析者，我仅限于指出后者的存在，展示其内容，并描述它们如何被考虑、或如何未被考虑。某些伦理问题处于被动化的核心。用一个被过度使用的术语来说，这就是我们所谓市场批判的根源。
THE PASSIVA(C)TION OF CERTAIN LIVING BEINGS
某些生命体的被动化

The difficulties raised by the market-oriented passiva(c)tion of nonhuman beings are just as great as those raised by the market-oriented passiva(c)tion of humans. The ongoing domestication of land and money have already proven striking illustrations.
非人存在者面向市场的被动化所引发的困难，与人类面向市场的被动化所引发的困难同样巨大。土地与货币持续进行的驯化，已经提供了引人注目的例证。

The opposition between humans and nonhumans, however, is too simple to encompass all cases. Populations that are being commoditized are more different and more varied than is generally supposed, and the borders do not necessarily lie where one expects them. Nonhumans are neither easier nor more difficult to tame, to put to work, and to frame (
cadrer

) than humans. Some of them resist domestication, while others bend to it without effective resistance. On both sides, one can in fact observe a whole range of behavior. Among non-humans it is, however, no doubt living beings that raise the most difficult problems, even if, as the chemical entity with which I will start proves, common nonhuman, nonliving entities can already cause considerable headaches.
然而，人与非人之间的对立过于简单，无法涵盖所有情形。正在被商品化的各类群体，比人们通常设想的更为不同、更为多样，边界也未必位于人们所期待的地方。非人并不比人更容易或更难被驯服、被投入工作、被框定（
cadrer
）。它们之中有些抵抗驯化，另一些则毫无有效抵抗地屈从于驯化。事实上，在双方身上都能观察到一整套行为。然而，在非人之中，最棘手的问题无疑是由生命体提出的，尽管正如我即将首先讨论的化学实体所证明的那样，普通的非人、非生命实体已经能够造成相当大的麻烦。

Chemical industries throughout their existence and their enormous growth have confronted the difficulties of framing the entities with which they flood the market. Some steps of their market-oriented passiva(c)tion are not particularly problematic. Chemical engineering is preoccupied only with organizing the production of molecules or combinations of molecules with their nexus of associations, which are easily detached from everything that contributes to producing and qualifying them. What a distillation column collects is, as the name indications, successfully disentangled. The distillate, thanks to chemical knowledge and technology, can continue its career without its origins and its biography weighing directly on the actions that it will enable: whether it is extracted from oil shale or passed through the hands of engineers working for multinational companies does not have direct consequences on the services it is able to offer.

化学工业在其整个存在和巨大增长过程中，一直面对着框定其倾泻到市场上的各种实体的困难。其面向市场的被动化的某些步骤并不特别成问题。化学工程只关心组织分子或分子组合的生产，连同其关联网络，而这些分子很容易从一切有助于生产和界定其品质的事物中脱离出来。蒸馏塔所收集的东西，正如其名称所示，被成功地解缠了。得益于化学知识与技术，馏出物能够继续其生涯，而其起源与传记不会直接压在其将促成的行动之上：无论它是从油页岩中提取的，还是经过为跨国公司工作的工程师之手，都不会直接影响它所能提供的服务。

Although the detachment of these chemical beings, however complex it may be, is not out of reach, the same cannot be said of the task of managing their behavior once they exit the plants and begin their autonomous lives. Substances and chemical products are goods whose quasi-natural propensity is to react, to enter into new combinations, to catalyze, to migrate, to transform themselves or embed themselves, to pollute, and these actions are not entirely predictable or subject to discipline. The lead that the oil industry uses to improve fuel performance endlessly contaminates the planet, and plastic is colonizing the oceans. By making available substances that have duly been detached and are easy to alienate, but are still very active, the chemical industry constantly runs the risk of losing control over them, of no longer being able to ensure the delicate balance between autonomy, which remains within the framework set out for these substances, and recurrent slippages, which overflow the framework. This is no doubt why the chemical sector has such a hard time constructing a moral image for itself. The beings on which it works and that it puts into circulation are hard to educate properly.
Despite all the precautions taken or incompletely taken, they provoke disorder. This ambivalence is due to their very being, which is riven by uncertainties that can be considered ontological.

尽管这些化学存在者的脱离无论多么复杂，并非遥不可及，但一旦它们离开工厂、开始自主生活，管理其行为这项任务却并非如此。物质与化学产品是这样一类物品：其准自然的倾向就是发生反应、进入新的组合、催化、迁移、自我转化或将自身嵌入某处、造成污染，而这些行动并不完全可预测，也不完全服从规训。石油工业用来提高燃料性能的铅不断地污染着地球，塑料正在殖民海洋。化学工业通过提供那些已经适当脱离、易于让渡、但仍然十分活跃的物质，不断冒着失去对它们控制的风险，冒着再也无法确保自主性与反复出现的滑移之间微妙平衡的风险——前者仍处于为这些物质设定的框架之内，后者则溢出框架。这无疑正是化学部门如此难以为自己构建道德形象的原因。它所加工并投入流通的存在者很难被恰当地教育。
尽管采取了或未完全采取种种预防措施，它们仍会制造混乱。这种矛盾性源于它们的存在本身，其存在被种种可被视为本体论的不确定性所撕裂。

The commodification process becomes even more problematic as one moves from chemicals into the world of living beings. Indeed, if we consider only the careers of so-called inert entities and their instrumental uses, we would miss the new actions and novel outlets that have opened up around living entities. The living, whether human or nonhuman, has the huge advantage of being creative, good at multitasking, adaptive, evolving, even if, like money, it has the frightening drawback of being more difficult to maintain within a framework. The stakes are such that the coming decades may well become a time when the passiva(c)tion of the living processes becomes more intense. This is a necessary prelude to their commodification.

随着我们从化学品转入生命体的世界，商品化过程变得更加棘手。的确，如果我们只考虑所谓惰性实体的生涯及其工具性用途，就会错过围绕生命体展开的新行动与新出路。生命体，无论人还是非人，都具有巨大的优势：富有创造性、善于多任务处理、适应性强、能够演化；即便它和货币一样，也有一个可怕的缺点——更难被维持在某个框架之内。利害关系如此之大，以至于未来数十年很可能成为一个生命过程的被动化变得更为激烈的时期。这是其商品化的必要前奏。

The living reproduces itself, develops, and evolves, permanent cellular regeneration being a condition for all these characteristics. How can one make such beings available without paralyzing their capacity to
make others act

and to provoke new courses of action, at least for a moment, in those who become attached to them? There is no reason to think that what has been possible for the human being cannot be achieved with less complicated living beings or even with assemblages of machines and human beings such as those offered by service providers.
生命体自我繁殖、发育并演化，而持续的细胞再生是所有这些特征的条件。如何使这样的存在者变得可得，同时又不麻痹它们的能力——即
让他者行动
、并在那些附着于它们的人身上至少暂时引发新行动方案的能力？没有理由认为，对人已经可能做到的事，就不能在更不复杂的生命体身上实现，甚至不能在由服务提供者提供的机器与人的装配中实现。

Indeed, as far as animals are concerned, we are not starting from scratch. The most extreme and perhaps also the oldest form of their passiva(c)tion is the one that, by stripping or denying them of their condition as living beings, transforms them into food for humans. Over the course of time, this project has constantly become organized and more complex, forming a long chain of activities that take place in different sites and that mobilize a wide range of know-how, techniques, and organizations. Through successive stages, it leads a cow or a sheep frolicking in a green pasture or bored to tears in an industrial stable to lie quietly, in the form of leg of lamb, sirloin steak, or tripe
à la mode de Caen

, waiting for a client who will let himself be tempted enough to pull out his wallet before savoring them at home. The operations involved in disentangling are well known: begin by reducing the animal to a quasi-automaton in industrial stables that have openings organized for it to be able to contemplate the milieu from which it has been torn, calm it when taking it out of its factory, and then, sometimes using the services of an animal decoy, a sort of collaborating double agent in man’s service to lead the way (and which will be spared in order for it to repeat this ignominious task), lead the animal to the truck, slaughter it, skin it, gut it, put aside the spinal column and “risky” offal to end up with half carcasses or quartered ones. Then the muscles must be separated to remove the membrane, superficial fat, and connected bones. Finally, the pieces must be put into groups based on types of muscle and vacuum packed. Thus requalified as meat ready to be cut, made into pieces, and perhaps put into plastic containers for retail sale, the animal is finally ready to enter into new courses of action, such as a thoughtfully organized birthday dinner for grandma, who will enthuse over how tender the roast beef is or how skilled the butcher. What is fascinating about this story, a long-running story that helped populate the planet with domestic animals, is that this process has evolved continuously, as though nothing were ever to be taken for granted. The contents of supply and demand are constantly reworked and readjusted, the same problem always requiring a solution: disentangling the good, detaching it, and profiling it so that it can easily enter into more and more singular courses of action.
的确，就动物而言，我们并非从零开始。其被动化最极端、或许也是最古老的形式，是剥夺或否认它们作为生命体的状况，把它们转化为人的食物。随着时间推移，这一工程不断组织化、复杂化，形成一条漫长的活动链，这些活动发生在不同场所，并调动广泛多样的技能、技术与组织。经过接连不断的阶段，它把一头在绿色牧场上欢跳、或在工业化畜栏中烦闷欲死的牛或羊，引向以羊腿、西冷牛排或卡昂风味牛肚（tripe
à la mode de Caen

）的形式静静躺着，等待一位顾客，这位顾客会被诱惑得足以掏出钱包，然后在家中细细品尝。解缠所涉及的操作是众所周知的：首先把动物还原为工业化畜栏中的准自动机——畜栏设有专门安排的开口，使它能够凝望自己被拽离的环境；在把它带出工厂时让它平静下来；然后，有时借助一头动物诱饵——一个为人类效劳、负责领路的合作双面间谍（它会被免于宰杀，以便重复这项不光彩的任务）——把动物引向卡车，宰杀、剥皮、取出内脏，把脊柱和“有风险”的下水放到一边，最终得到半胴体或四分之一胴体。接着必须分离肌肉，去除筋膜、表层脂肪和相连的骨骼。最后，必须按肌肉类型把肉块分组并进行真空包装。动物由此被重新界定为可供切割、分块、或许还装入塑料盒供零售的肉，终于准备好进入新的行动方案，例如一场精心筹办的祖母生日晚宴——祖母会赞叹烤牛肉多么鲜嫩，或者屠夫多么手艺高超。这个故事——一个长期上演、帮助让家畜遍布地球的故事——令人着迷之处在于，这一过程持续演化，仿佛一切从来都不能被当作理所当然。供给与需求的内容不断被重新加工和调整，同一个问题始终需要解决方案：解缠物品、使其脱离，并刻画其特征，以便它能轻易进入越来越独一的行动方案。

At the same time, in parallel to human beings, tamed and domesticated animals have been gradually put to task and transformed into workforce — for instance, to provide milk or as pack animals — that could be involved in market transactions. Millions of horses and mules sold to the military died on the battlefield during the Great War.

It used to be that one rented the services of ox teams. Servicing by bulls is still for sale. More and more dogs trained to lead the blind will be sold, as will capuchin monkeys who can assist muscular dystrophy patients with daily tasks, thus entering into competition with human caregivers. When the very programming mechanisms of life are targeted, as is the case with biotechnologies that act on its most intimate dynamics, there seems to be no limit to the ways living beings can be put to work. There are, however, innumerable difficulties, since domestication and the controls it requires always raise daunting problems and often raise numerous objections.
与此同时，与人并行，被驯服和家养的动物逐渐被投入劳作，转化为可以参与市场交易的劳动力——例如提供牛奶，或充当驮畜。第一次世界大战期间，数以百万计卖给军队的马和骡子死于战场。
过去人们会租用牛队的服务。公牛提供的配种服务至今仍在出售。越来越多经过训练、能为盲人引路的狗将被出售，能协助肌营养不良症患者完成日常任务的卷尾猴也将被出售，从而与人类护理者展开竞争。当生命自身的编程机制成为目标时——正如作用于生命最内在动态的生物技术那样——生命体被投入工作的方式似乎就没有限度了。然而，困难不胜枚举，因为驯化及其所需的控制总是提出令人生畏的问题，并常常招致众多反对。

A striking illustration of the complexity of these market-oriented passiva(c)tion processes is provided by the genetically modified organisms (GMOs) that are invading the food and health care industries (plants and seeds, therapeutic genes, tissues, cells and organs, and so on). For each of these beings, a compromise must be found; it is difficult to strike, since what makes them of interest is their capacity to act and react, while their commodification is possible only if these qualities are limited to some extent, domesticated, made predictable, and if the capacity inherent in life to overflow set frameworks can be brought under control.
这些面向市场的被动化过程的复杂性，有一个引人注目的例证：转基因生物（GMOs）正侵入食品与医疗保健产业（植物与种子、治疗性基因、组织、细胞与器官等等）。对每一种这样的存在者，都必须找到一种妥协；而这种妥协难以达成，因为使它们具有价值的，正是其行动与反应的能力，而它们的商品化只有在这些品质于某种程度上受到限制、被驯化、变得可预测，并且生命固有的溢出既定框架的能力能够受到控制时，才可能实现。
There are numerous examples of this evolution and the devices it requires, if only to ensure that the sanitary and environmental effects of the commercialized products are under control.

I will simply mention the telling case of plant seeds. These are indeed living organisms in the very ordinary sense of the term, since they are capable of reproducing themselves. Reproduction generally brings modifications (either deliberately or spontaneously), and these modifications, even if they are very useful for selection operations, have the serious drawback that they sometimes make the seeds so unpredictable that their transformation into commodities becomes problematic. To get around this difficulty, the (regulatory) notion of plant variety was introduced.

A variety is defined by the homogeneity of the plants considered and by the stability of their characteristics over reproductive cycles. Obtaining these properties, which requires a lot of work and which is sanctioned by institutional recognition, provides a perfect illustration of the process involved in the passiva(c)tion of goods. Once they are put into circulation, the seeds continue to act, as indeed they must, since it is asked of them that they produce new harvests. Nothing attaches them any longer either to those who produced them or to the conditions of their production; they live their own existence autonomously while behaving predictably. They are available to enter market transactions. This device is all the more original and efficient because having been created and stabilized (that is to say, duly passiva(c)ted), the variety is made available to farmers who are authorized to engage it in crossbreeding and selection operations in order to give rise to new varieties that will in turn be passiva(c)ted. Life is thus given the chance to exercise its creative force in a slow and controlled way. At the same time, some of life’s states are temporarily frozen so as to make it possible to establish temporarily stable market agencements.
这种演化及其所需装置的例证不胜枚举，哪怕只是为了确保商业化产品在卫生与环境方面的效应受到控制。
我只想提一提植物种子这个很有说服力的例子。种子确实是该词最平常意义上的生命体，因为它们能够自我繁殖。繁殖通常会带来改变（有意的或自发的），而这些改变尽管对选育操作十分有用，却有一个严重缺点：它们有时会使种子变得如此不可预测，以致其转化为商品成为问题。为了绕开这一困难，人们引入了植物品种这一（监管性）概念。

一个品种由所涉植物的同质性及其性状在繁殖周期中的稳定性来界定。获得这些属性需要大量工作，并须得到制度性承认，这为物品被动化所涉及的过程提供了完美例证。种子一旦投入流通，便继续行动——它们也确实必须如此，因为人们要求它们产出新的收成。它们不再附着于生产它们的人，也不再附着于其生产条件；它们自主地过着自己的存在，同时表现得可预测。它们随时可以进入市场交易。这一装置之所以格外原创而有效，是因为品种在被创造并稳定（也就是说，被适当地被动化）之后，被提供给农民，农民则获准将其用于杂交和选育操作，以产生新的品种，而这些新品种又将被被动化。生命由此获得机会，以一种缓慢而可控的方式施展其创造力。与此同时，生命的某些状态被暂时冻结，以便能够建立暂时稳定的市场装配。

Manufacturing such varieties is not simple. Considerable investments were required to obtain them and ensure their sustainability while leaving room for the creative process to begin anew. This has taken numerous experiments, both in laboratories and in open fields. It required developing regulations and then negotiating to have them accepted, setting up surveillance mechanisms and conservation arrangements. Persistence has paid off. These efforts have been crowned by the legally sanctioned certificate of plant variety protection (Certificat d’Obtention Végétale, COV). It defines and imposes plant qualities that allow them to be recognized as varieties and prepares them to become goods . . . ready for the market.

制造这样的品种并不简单。为获得它们并确保其可持续性，同时为创造过程重新开始留出空间，需要可观的投资。这需要在实验室和露天田地里进行大量实验。它要求制定规则，然后通过谈判使规则获得接受，建立监督机制和保存安排。坚持不懈终有回报。这些努力最终以法律认可的植物品种保护证书（Certificat d’Obtention Végétale，COV）而告成。该证书界定并强制规定植物的品质，使它们能够被认定为品种，并使它们准备好成为物品……随时可以进入市场。

And yet even as it seemed that a durable solution had been found to the problem of plant passiva(c)tion, the delicate equilibrium on which it was based was upset by scientists and engineers. The living never cease to be a surprise. Until recently, the selectors, whether they started their work with known varieties or not, were not supposed to add anything to the abundant mechanisms through which nature crossbreeds and selects species. If they wanted to transform the seeds into commercial goods, their ambition and competence did not extend beyond organizing the process wisely, channeling it so as to ensure the stability of the species obtained. With the development of transgenic techniques, selectors no longer simply organize natural processes intelligently. They intervene directly in the genome in order to create plants that are, for example, able to repel the attacks of certain insects, resist the aggressions of powerful herbicides, withstand drought, or manufacture molecules with therapeutic uses. The entity thus transformed can make appear and make possible in a sudden rapid way unprecedented courses of action; therein lies its interest. The increased activation of the plant is, of course, an advantage, but it is also the source of weaknesses. The seed of a genetically modified plant, because it is the result of suspending the mechanisms of natural selection, represents a leap into the unknown. It becomes a suspicious object. Having been obtained by novel means, the new entity inevitably generates problems of control and mastery for which there are no ready-made solutions.
The uncertainty as to the consequences that may result for the environment and for health reach their zenith: the seed becomes the object of concern.

然而，就在人们似乎已经为植物被动化问题找到了持久解决方案之时，这一方案所依赖的微妙平衡却被科学家和工程师打乱了。生命从不停止给人惊喜。直到不久以前，选育者无论是否从已知品种开始工作，都不应给大自然杂交和选择物种的丰富机制增添任何东西。如果他们想把种子转化为商业物品，其抱负和能力也不过是明智地组织这一过程，对其加以引导，以确保所得物种的稳定性。随着转基因技术的发展，选育者不再只是明智地组织自然过程。他们直接干预基因组，以创造出例如能够击退某些昆虫攻击、抵抗强力除草剂侵袭、耐受干旱或制造具有治疗用途的分子的植物。如此被转化的实体能够以突然而迅速的方式让前所未有的行动方案显现并成为可能；其价值正在于此。植物被增强的激活当然是一种优势，但也是弱点的来源。转基因植物的种子，由于是悬置自然选择机制的结果，代表着向未知的一跃。它变成了一个可疑的对象。由于是以新方法获得的，这一新实体不可避免地产生控制和驾驭的问题，而对此并没有现成答案。
关于它可能对环境与健康造成何种后果的不确定性达到顶点：种子成为关切的对象。

Passiva(c)tion, elegantly obtained in the case of varieties whose stability and homogeneity was almost certainly ensured, becomes a constantly renewed formidable challenge. It raises a whole host of novel problems that it is far from simple to solve: how can one ensure that the modifications that have been introduced on purpose, forcing nature, will not provoke unexpected effects and collateral damage? How can they be identified and prevented? At what point does experimentation give way to perfectly predictable and well-framed production? Can one even still assert that there is a clear demarcation between these two phases? Is it not the case that exploitation is actually experimentation on a large scale? Seed passiva(c)tion is not only a real scientific and technical conundrum; it is also becoming a serious political preoccupation. Seeds can sow doubt and concern. Passiva(c)tion activities, which used to be invisible and ignored, are now in the limelight and at the heart of market activities and public debates. Controversies are in full swing, and consensus is elusive. GMPs (genetically modified plants) are problem beings that will probably never grow out of their adolescent crisis.

对于那些稳定性与同质性几乎可以肯定得到确保的品种，被动化被优雅地实现了；但如今它却变成一项不断更新的艰巨挑战。它提出了一大堆新颖的问题，而这些问题远非轻易可以解决：如何确保那些为了强行干预自然而刻意引入的改变不会引发意外效应和附带损害？如何识别并预防这些效应？实验在什么时候让位于完全可预测、框定良好的生产？人们甚至还能断言这两个阶段之间存在清晰的分界吗？难道开发利用实际上不就是大规模实验吗？种子的被动化不仅是一个真实的科学与技术难题，也正在成为一项严肃的政治关切。种子能够散播怀疑与忧虑。过去不可见、被忽视的被动化活动，如今处于聚光灯下，位于市场活动与公共辩论的核心。争论如火如荼，共识难以达成。转基因植物（GMPs）是问题存在者，很可能永远无法走出其青春期危机。

What goes for plant genomes also goes for human genomes; what goes for plant transgenesis also goes for gene therapy. Take the case of a genetic disease called X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency (X-SCID), which results from the malfunction of a single gene. It condemns affected newborns to living in a maximally isolated sterile environment, an artificial bubble, in order to avoid infections — hence the name bubble boy disease. Having identified the responsible gene, researchers decided to replace it with a gene drug. The latter is inserted, outside the organism (
ex vivo

), into the patient’s cells via a viral vector of the retrovirus type. This vector allows the gene to penetrate the cell and insert itself into the genome; the missing protein is thus produced in the children. Once this step has been accomplished, the corrected cells, which are the origin of the elements responsible for the immune system defenses (T lymphocytes), are reinjected into the patient. The first vector chosen for this task by Alain Fischer was a retrovirus that seemed to fit the bill perfectly. In trials, it turned out not to. Although it was efficient in most cases, reliably playing its part as a vector and simple transport mechanism, it induced leukemia in certain babies because it took the liberty of introducing itself near one of the genes that fosters cancers. It turned out that the virus more or less handles its job, but that like all living entities, it sometimes happens to do something other than what it is told to do, triggering unacceptable actions.
适用于植物基因组的，也适用于人类基因组；适用于植物转基因的，也适用于基因疗法。以一种名为X连锁重度联合免疫缺陷症（X-SCID）的遗传病为例，它由单个基因的功能失常引起。这种病迫使患病新生儿生活在最大限度隔离的无菌环境中，即一个人造气泡里，以避免感染——因此得名“气泡男孩病”。研究人员在确定致病基因后，决定用一种基因药物将其替换。这种基因药物在生物体外（
ex vivo
